```text
`V' := {pairEncode x u : |u| = C(|x|+1)^c ∧ x ++ u ∈ V}` with the same bound:
deciding `V'` parses the aligned pair (the `Turing.pairDecode` grammar; a
polynomial-time scan), checks the length equality against the explicit formula,
reassembles `x ++ u`, and runs `V`'s decider — each a named machine obligation
for the fill, none exotic. (⇐) From the bounded form `(C, c, V)`, take exact
length `R n = (C+1)(n+1)^c` — **admissible** for the repaired `NP`
(coefficient `C+1`, degree `c`; the round-2 audit refuted the earlier choice
`C(n+1)^c + 1`, which is not of the class's required shape — round-2
finding 1) — leaving `R n - C(n+1)^c = (n+1)^c ≥ 1` room for the marker. Pad
each certificate right-self-delimitingly to `u ++ [true] ++ false-run` of
length `R n`. The new verifier, on `y` of length `m`: search `n ≤ m` for
`n + R n = m` — strict increase of `n ↦ n + R n` gives **at most one**
solution, and none may exist (e.g. `y = []`, since `R n ≥ 1`): **reject if no
such `n` exists** (round-3 audit, finding 1); otherwise split `y = x ++ v` at
that unique `n` with
`|v| = R n ≥ 1`; reject if `v` has no `true` bit (so stripping never enters
`x`); split `v = u ++ [true] ++ false-run` at the **last** `true`; check the
*original* bound `|u| ≤ C(n+1)^c` — checkable precisely because the bound is
the explicit formula (phase-1 finding 2's residual error, fixed in round 1) —
and consult `V` on `pairEncode x u`. Every old witness pads within `R n`
(`|u| + 1 ≤ C(n+1)^c + 1 ≤ R n`); every accepted new witness strips back to
an old one (the round-2 audit's reconstruction, checked there across the
`C = 0`, `c = 0`, `x = []`, `u = []`, all-`false`, and malformed edge
cases). -/
theorem mem_NP_iff_exists_length_le {L : Language Bool} :
    L ∈ NP ↔ ∃ (C c : ℕ) (V : Language Bool), V ∈ P ∧
      ∀ x : List Bool, x ∈ L ↔
        ∃ u : List Bool, u.length ≤ C * (x.length + 1) ^ c ∧ pairEncode x u ∈ V  := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨C, c, V, hV, hL⟩
    refine ⟨C, c, pairedVerifier C c V, ?_, fun x => ?_⟩
    · -- Remaining machine obligation: aligned parsing, the explicit polynomial
      -- length-equality test, concatenation, and timed execution of V's decider.
      exact pairedVerifier_mem_P C c hV
    · rw [hL x]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨u, hu, hVu⟩
        exact ⟨u, hu.le, (pairedVerifier_pair C c V x u).mpr ⟨hu, hVu⟩⟩
      · rintro ⟨u, -, hVu⟩
        exact ⟨u, (pairedVerifier_pair C c V x u).mp hVu⟩
  · rintro ⟨C, c, V, hV, hL⟩
    refine ⟨C + 1, c, paddedVerifier C c V, ?_, fun x => ?_⟩
    · -- Remaining machine obligation: bounded split search, last-true stripping,
      -- the original-bound test, pairing, and timed execution of V's decider.
      exact paddedVerifier_mem_P C c hV
    · exact (hL x).trans (paddedVerifier_witness C c V x).symm

end Complexity
```


## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/ClassNP/CoNP.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.NP

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The class coNP

[AB09, §2.6.1]: `coNP` is the class of complements of `NP` languages
(Definition 2.19), equivalently the class of languages whose membership is
certified by *every* polynomial-length certificate (Definition 2.20); the
equivalence is [AB09, Exercise 2.24]. This module also records the closure of
`P` under complement that the equivalence rides on, and the two standard
containment facts `P ⊆ NP ∩ coNP` and `P = NP → NP = coNP`.

## Design

* The complement-form Definition 2.19 is primary (it is one line); the
  ∀-certificate form is the characterization theorem, matching [AB09]'s own
  pedagogical ordering in reverse.
* `Complexity.compl_mem_P` is a statement *about the Chapter-1 class `P`* that
  Chapter 1 never needed; it is a new addition beyond the audited Chapter-1
  surface, placed here (its first consumer) and flagged for the phase-1 audit.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.coNP` — the class coNP. [AB09, Definition 2.19]

## Main results

* `Complexity.compl_mem_P` — `P` is closed under complement.
* `Complexity.mem_coNP_iff_forall` — the ∀-certificate characterization
  [AB09, Definition 2.20 and Exercise 2.24].
* `Complexity.P_subset_NP_inter_coNP` — [AB09, Exercise 2.23].
* `Complexity.NP_eq_coNP_of_P_eq_NP` — [AB09, Exercise 2.25].

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§2.6.1, Definitions 2.19-2.20, pp. 55-56;
  Exercises 2.23-2.25.)
-/

namespace Complexity

/-- **The class coNP** [AB09, Definition 2.19]: the complements of `NP` languages. -/
def coNP : Set (Language Bool) :=
  {L | Lᶜ ∈ NP}

/-- **`P` is closed under complement**: if `L` is decidable in polynomial time then
so is its complement.

**Proof sketch.** Obtain a decider of `L` from `Complexity.mem_P_iff`, read it
pointwise as computing the total singleton-indicator function (the decider's
output is exactly `[indicator L x]`), and postcompose with the Boolean-negation
postprocessor `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_ifEq [true] [false] [true]`
(`w ↦ if w = [true] then [false] else [true]`) via the **timed** total
composition `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_comp` — the untimed
`exists_comp_partial` carries no time bound (phase-1 audit, finding 4). The
composite computes the complement's indicator within a budget polynomial by the
composition ledger and the monotonicity of the explicit polynomial; return
through `Complexity.mem_P_of_dtime_le`. Buffered composition keeps the
intermediate bit off the real output. This is a new statement about the
Chapter-1 class, flagged for audit (plan §6) and certified by the phase-1
round (finding 10). -/
theorem compl_mem_P {L : Language Bool} (h : L ∈ P) : Lᶜ ∈ P := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨C, d, M, hM⟩ := mem_P_iff.mp h
  obtain ⟨N, a, hN⟩ := Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_ifEq [true] [false] [true]
  have hfun : M.ComputesFunInTime (fun x => [Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator L x])
      (fun n => C * (n + 1) ^ d) := fun x => hM x
  -- Buffer the decider's singleton output and apply the timed Boolean postprocessor.
  obtain ⟨M', b, hcomp⟩ := Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_comp
    hfun hN
    (fun _ _ hle => Nat.mul_le_mul_left a (Nat.add_le_add_right hle 1))
  have hdec : M'.DecidesInTime Lᶜ
      (fun n => b * (C * (n + 1) ^ d + a * (C * (n + 1) ^ d + 1) + 1)) := by
    intro x
    by_cases hx : x ∈ L
    · have hxc : x ∉ (Lᶜ : Language Bool) := fun hnot => hnot hx
      simpa [Function.comp_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, hx, hxc] using hcomp x
    · have hxc : x ∈ (Lᶜ : Language Bool) := hx
      simpa [Function.comp_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, hx, hxc] using hcomp x
  -- Absorb the linear postprocessor and composition overhead into the same degree.
  refine mem_P_of_dtime_le
    (T := fun n => b * (C * (n + 1) ^ d + a * (C * (n + 1) ^ d + 1) + 1))
    ⟨1, M', by simpa only [one_mul] using hdec⟩
    (b * (C + a * (C + 1) + 1) * 2 ^ d) d ?_
  intro n
  have hpow : 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ d := Nat.pow_pos (Nat.succ_pos n)
  have hsum : C * (n + 1) ^ d + 1 ≤ (C + 1) * (n + 1) ^ d := by
    calc C * (n + 1) ^ d + 1 ≤ C * (n + 1) ^ d + (n + 1) ^ d :=
        Nat.add_le_add_left hpow _
      _ = (C + 1) * (n + 1) ^ d := by ring
  calc b * (C * (n + 1) ^ d + a * (C * (n + 1) ^ d + 1) + 1)
      ≤ b * (C * (n + 1) ^ d + a * ((C + 1) * (n + 1) ^ d) + (n + 1) ^ d) :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul_left b
          (Nat.add_le_add (Nat.add_le_add_left (Nat.mul_le_mul_left a hsum) _) hpow)
    _ = b * (C + a * (C + 1) + 1) * (n + 1) ^ d := by ring
    _ ≤ b * (C + a * (C + 1) + 1) * (2 ^ d * (n ^ d + 1)) :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (succ_pow_le n d)
    _ = b * (C + a * (C + 1) + 1) * 2 ^ d * (n ^ d + 1) := by ring

/-- **The ∀-certificate characterization of coNP** [AB09, Definition 2.20,
equivalence per Exercise 2.24]: `L ∈ coNP` iff there are a certificate
coefficient `C`, degree `c`, and a verifier `V ∈ P` with
`x ∈ L ↔ ∀ u, |u| = C(|x|+1)^c → x ++ u ∈ V` — the same explicit length
formula as `Complexity.NP` (phase-1 audit repair, finding 1).

**Proof sketch.** Negate the exact-length existential in `NP`'s membership
equivalence for `Lᶜ`: `x ∈ L ↔ ¬(∃ u, |u| = C(|x|+1)^c ∧ x ++ u ∈ V₀)
↔ ∀ u, |u| = C(|x|+1)^c → x ++ u ∈ V₀ᶜ`, and `V₀ᶜ ∈ P` by
`Complexity.compl_mem_P`; both directions instantiate the same `C, c`,
complementing the verifier. Purely logical — no certificate-length computation
is needed (audit finding table). -/
theorem mem_coNP_iff_forall {L : Language Bool} :
    L ∈ coNP ↔ ∃ (C c : ℕ) (V : Language Bool), V ∈ P ∧
      ∀ x : List Bool, x ∈ L ↔
        ∀ u : List Bool, u.length = C * (x.length + 1) ^ c → x ++ u ∈ V := by
  classical
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨C, c, V, hV, hmem⟩
    refine ⟨C, c, Vᶜ, compl_mem_P hV, fun x => ?_⟩
    have hx : x ∉ L ↔ ∃ u : List Bool,
        u.length = C * (x.length + 1) ^ c ∧ x ++ u ∈ V := hmem x
    change x ∈ L ↔ ∀ u : List Bool,
      u.length = C * (x.length + 1) ^ c → x ++ u ∉ V
    simpa only [not_not, not_exists, not_and] using not_congr hx
  · rintro ⟨C, c, V, hV, hmem⟩
    refine ⟨C, c, Vᶜ, compl_mem_P hV, fun x => ?_⟩
    change x ∉ L ↔ ∃ u : List Bool,
      u.length = C * (x.length + 1) ^ c ∧ x ++ u ∉ V
    simpa only [not_forall, exists_prop] using not_congr (hmem x)

/-- **`P ⊆ NP ∩ coNP`** [AB09, Exercise 2.23].

**Proof sketch.** `P ⊆ NP` is `Complexity.P_subset_NP`; for the `coNP` half,
`L ∈ P` gives `Lᶜ ∈ P ⊆ NP` by `Complexity.compl_mem_P`, i.e. `L ∈ coNP`. -/
theorem P_subset_NP_inter_coNP : P ⊆ NP ∩ coNP := by
  intro L hL
  exact ⟨P_subset_NP hL, P_subset_NP (compl_mem_P hL)⟩

/-- **If `P = NP` then `NP = coNP`** [AB09, Exercise 2.25].

**Proof sketch.** Under `P = NP`: `L ∈ NP → L ∈ P → Lᶜ ∈ P → Lᶜ ∈ NP → L ∈ coNP`
by `Complexity.compl_mem_P`, and symmetrically `L ∈ coNP → Lᶜ ∈ NP = P → L ∈ P =
NP` by closing under complement once more. -/
theorem NP_eq_coNP_of_P_eq_NP (h : P = NP) : NP = coNP := by
  apply Set.Subset.antisymm
  · intro L hL
    change Lᶜ ∈ NP
    rw [← h] at hL ⊢
    exact compl_mem_P hL
  · intro L hL
    change Lᶜ ∈ NP at hL
    rw [← h] at hL ⊢
    simpa only [compl_compl] using compl_mem_P hL

end Complexity
```


## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/ClassNP/PolyTimeBlockTests.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 The TCSlib Authors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib Contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimeBlockLoop

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The aggregated block tests

The three customers of the bounded block-query loop
(`TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimeBlockLoop`): the one-bit OR,
strict-majority, and XOR-then-OR aggregations of a polynomial-time one-bit
indicator over polynomially many polynomial-length blocks are polynomial-time.
Each is an instance of the countdown block loop `Complexity.BlockLoop`
(`PolyTimeBlockLoop`), with the aggregation state (flag, vote counters, XOR mask)
carried inside the loop's state word.  The XOR-then-OR test is an instance of the
OR-flag engine `Complexity.BlockLoop.polyTimeComputable_orLoop`, supplying its per-round
test, its remainder update and the closed form of its remainders; the plain OR test is
the XOR-then-OR test with an all-`false` mask.

These are the `PolyTimeComputable` engines of the `P`-closure lemmas
`Complexity.mem_P_of_blockAny` / `_blockMajority` / `_blockXorAny` in
`TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PClosure`.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.blockAt` — the `i`-th length-`a·(n+1)^k` block of the second
  component of a pair, where `n` is the first component's length.

## Main results

* `Complexity.BlockLoop.polyTimeComputable_orLoop` — the OR-flag block loop is
  polynomial-time, and its output is the OR of the per-round tests.
* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_blockAnyTest` / `_blockXorAnyTest` — the
  aggregated one-bit OR and XOR-then-OR block tests of a polynomial-time
  one-bit indicator are polynomial-time.  The strict-majority test lives in
  `TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimeBlockMajority`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§7.3, Theorem 7.8; §7.4.1; Theorems
  7.14–7.15: the implicit "simulate the machine on each block" closures.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- The `i`-th length-`a·(n+1)^k` block of the second component of a pair,
where `n` is the first component's length. -/
def blockAt (a k : ℕ) (z : List Bool) (i : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  ((pairSndD z).drop (i * (a * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k))).take
    (a * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k)

/-! #### The OR-flag block loop -/

namespace BlockLoop

/-- Replacing a nonempty word by the flag `[true]` does not lengthen it. -/
theorem length_flag_le {f : List Bool} (hf : f ≠ []) (b : Bool) :
    (if b then [true] else f).length ≤ f.length := by
  cases b
  · simp
  · simpa using List.length_pos_of_ne_nil hf

/-- One OR round: raising the flag on the `i`-th test value extends the flag
`[(range i).any F]` to `[(range (i+1)).any F]`. -/
theorem any_range_succ_flag (F : ℕ → Bool) (i : ℕ) :
    (if F i then [true] else [(List.range i).any F]) = [(List.range (i + 1)).any F] := by
  rw [List.range_succ, List.any_append]
  cases h : F i <;> simp [h]

/-- **An OR-flag block loop computes the OR of its tests in polynomial time.**  Run from
`⟨[false], ⟨1^K z, r z⟩⟩`, `K z = a'·(|x z|+1)^k'`, the loop raising its flag when `t` holds
of the remainder and advancing the remainder by `nxt`.  If the remainders follow `Q z`
(`r z = Q z 0`, `nxt (Q z i) = Q z (i+1)`), `t (Q z i) = F z i`, `|nxt q| ≤ |q| + 2 + c`,
`|x z| ≤ |r z|`, and `t`, `nxt`, `x`, `r` are polynomial-time, then so is
`z ↦ [(range (K z)).any (F z)]`.
**Proof sketch.** `polyTimeComputable_countdown` with the flag update and `out = pairFstD`;
`loop_output` at heads `[(range i).any (F z)]`, by `any_range_succ_flag`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_orLoop {t : List Bool → Bool} {nxt x r : List Bool → List Bool}
    (Q : List Bool → ℕ → List Bool) {F : List Bool → ℕ → Bool} (a' k' c : ℕ)
    (ht : PolyTimeComputable (fun s => [t (pairSndD (pairSndD s))]))
    (hn : PolyTimeComputable (fun s => nxt (pairSndD (pairSndD s))))
    (hx : PolyTimeComputable x) (hr : PolyTimeComputable r)
    (hnlen : ∀ q, (nxt q).length ≤ q.length + 2 + c)
    (hxr : ∀ z, (x z).length ≤ (r z).length)
    (hQ0 : ∀ z, r z = Q z 0)
    (hadv : ∀ z i, i < a' * ((x z).length + 1) ^ k' → nxt (Q z i) = Q z (i + 1))
    (htest : ∀ z i, i < a' * ((x z).length + 1) ^ k' → t (Q z i) = F z i) :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [(List.range (a' * ((x z).length + 1) ^ k')).any (F z)]) := by
  refine polyTimeComputable_countdown
    (g := step (fun h q => if t q then [true] else h) (fun _ q => nxt q)) (out := pairFstD)
    rfl rfl [false] a' k' c (polyTimeComputable_ite ht (polyTimeComputable_const [true])
      polyTimeComputable_pairFstD) hn polyTimeComputable_pairFstD hx hr
    (fun h q hh => by
      have := length_flag_le hh (t q)
      have := hnlen q
      omega) (fun z => ?_)
  have hlen : (x z).length ≤ (pairEncode [false] (pairEncode
      (List.replicate (a' * ((x z).length + 1) ^ k') true) (r z))).length := by
    have := hxr z
    simp only [length_pairEncode]
    omega
  have hout := loop_output
    (g := step (fun h q => if t q then [true] else h) (fun _ q => nxt q)) (out := pairFstD)
    (s₀ := pairEncode [false] (pairEncode
      (List.replicate (a' * ((x z).length + 1) ^ k') true) (r z)))
    rfl (fun i => [(List.range i).any (F z)]) (Q z) (by simp [hQ0 z]) (fun _ _ => by simp)
    (fun i hi => by simp only [htest z i hi]; exact any_range_succ_flag (F z) i)
    (fun i hi => hadv z i hi) (lt_polyBudget_of_le a' k' hlen)
  rw [hout, pairFstD_pairEncode]

end BlockLoop

/-! #### The XOR-then-OR test -/

/-- The XOR-then-OR aggregated block test of a polynomial-time one-bit
indicator is polynomial-time: the input is a nested pair
`⟨⟨x, u⟩, v⟩`; block `i` is drawn from `u`, XORed bitwise with `v`
(truncating, `Complexity.xorD`), and tested paired with `x`.

**Proof sketch.** An instance of `Complexity.BlockLoop.polyTimeComputable_orLoop` on
the remainder `⟨v, ⟨x, u⟩⟩`: the round's test input is
`pairEncode x (xorD (pairEncode v block))` (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_xorD`,
`Complexity.xorD_pairEncode`), the mask `v` is carried unchanged, and the block is
dropped from `u`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_blockXorAnyTest {V : Language Bool}
    (hV : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [MultiTapeTM.indicator V z]))
    (a k a' k' : ℕ) :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun w =>
      [(List.range (a' * ((pairFstD (pairFstD w)).length + 1) ^ k')).any
        (fun i => MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD (pairFstD w))
          (List.zipWith xor (pairSndD w) (blockAt a k (pairFstD w) i))))]) := by
  have hzzz : PolyTimeComputable (fun s => pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD s))) :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp
      (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  have hmask : PolyTimeComputable (fun s => pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s))) :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp
      (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  have hx : PolyTimeComputable (fun w => pairFstD (pairFstD w)) :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD
  exact BlockLoop.polyTimeComputable_orLoop
    (t := fun q => MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD (pairSndD q))
      (xorD (pairEncode (pairFstD q) (pairSndD (sliceTakeAt a k (pairSndD q)))))))
    (nxt := fun q => pairEncode (pairFstD q) (sliceDropAt a k (pairSndD q)))
    (fun w i => pairEncode (pairSndD w) (pairEncode (pairFstD (pairFstD w))
      ((pairSndD (pairFstD w)).drop (i * (a * ((pairFstD (pairFstD w)).length + 1) ^ k)))))
    a' k' 2
    (hV.comp ((polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp hzzz).pairEncode
      (polyTimeComputable_xorD.comp (hmask.pairEncode
        (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp ((polyTimeComputable_sliceTakeAt a k).comp hzzz))))))
    (hmask.pairEncode ((polyTimeComputable_sliceDropAt a k).comp hzzz)) hx
    (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.pairEncode
      (hx.pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD)))
    (fun q => by
      have := length_sliceDropAt_le a k (pairSndD q)
      have := length_pair_components_le q
      rw [length_pairEncode]
      omega)
    (fun w => by simp only [length_pairEncode]; omega)
    (fun w => by simp)
    (fun w i _ => by
      simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, BlockLoop.sliceDropAt_pairEncode_drop])
    (fun w i _ => by
      simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, BlockLoop.sliceTakeAt_pairEncode_drop,
        xorD_pairEncode]
      rfl)

/-! #### The OR test as the XOR test with a zero mask -/

/-- XOR of a word with itself is the all-`false` word of its length. -/
private theorem zipWith_xor_self (l : List Bool) :
    List.zipWith xor l l = List.replicate l.length false := by
  induction l with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b l _ => simp [List.replicate_succ]

/-- XOR with an all-`false` mask of the block length leaves a block unchanged. -/
private theorem zipWith_xor_blockAt (a k : ℕ) (z : List Bool) (i : ℕ) :
    List.zipWith xor (List.replicate (a * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k) false)
      (blockAt a k z i) = blockAt a k z i := by
  have h : (blockAt a k z i).length ≤ a * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k :=
    List.length_take_le _ _
  generalize blockAt a k z i = l at h ⊢
  generalize a * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k = n at h ⊢
  induction l generalizing n with
  | nil => simp
  | cons b l ih =>
    cases n with
    | zero => simp at h
    | succ n =>
      rw [List.replicate_succ, List.zipWith_cons_cons, ih n (by simpa using h)]
      simp

/-- The OR-aggregated block test of a polynomial-time one-bit indicator is
polynomial-time: one bit saying whether some of the `a'·(n+1)^k'` blocks of
length `a·(n+1)^k` passes the test on `Turing.pairEncode`d (first component,
block).

**Proof sketch.** The XOR-then-OR test with an all-`false` mask of the block length:
on `⟨z, 0^B⟩`, where `B = a·(|x|+1)^k`, the XOR-shifted blocks are the blocks of `z`
themselves (each has length at most `B`), so this test is
`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_blockXorAnyTest` composed with `z ↦ ⟨z, 0^B⟩`.  The mask
`0^B` is computed as `xorD ⟨1^B, 1^B⟩` (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_polyUnary`,
`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_xorD`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_blockAnyTest {V : Language Bool}
    (hV : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [MultiTapeTM.indicator V z]))
    (a k a' k' : ℕ) :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun z =>
      [(List.range (a' * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k')).any
        (fun i => MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z i)))]) := by
  have hU : PolyTimeComputable
      (fun z => List.replicate (a * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k) true) :=
    (polyTimeComputable_polyUnary a k).comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD
  have hpad := polyTimeComputable_id.pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_xorD.comp (hU.pairEncode hU))
  convert (polyTimeComputable_blockXorAnyTest hV a k a' k').comp hpad using 1
  funext z
  simp only [Function.comp, id, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, xorD_pairEncode,
    zipWith_xor_self, List.length_replicate, zipWith_xor_blockAt]

end Complexity
```


## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/ClassNP/PolyTimeBlockMajority.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 The TCSlib Authors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib Contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimeBlockTests

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The majority-aggregated block test

The strict-majority customer of the bounded block-query loop
(`TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimeBlockLoop`), split from
`TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimeBlockTests` for size: an instance of the countdown
block loop `Complexity.BlockLoop` whose remainder carries two unary vote counters, and
whose chunk at countdown exhaustion is their strict comparison.

## Main definitions

None — the loop's round, chunk and initial state are private to this file.

## Main results

* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_blockMajorityTest` — the strict-majority
  aggregated one-bit block test of a polynomial-time one-bit indicator is
  polynomial-time.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§7.4.1, repeated trials with a majority
  vote; Theorem 7.14.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-! #### The majority-aggregating loop -/

/-- One round of the majority-aggregating block loop on state
`pairEncode [true] (pairEncode countdown (pairEncode (pairEncode uT uF)
(pairEncode x rem)))`: push one vote onto the passed (`uT`) or failed (`uF`)
unary counter according to the indicator of the current block, drop the
block, decrement the countdown.  An instance of `Complexity.BlockLoop.step` with the
live marker `[true]` as head. -/
private noncomputable def majStep (V : Language Bool) (a k : ℕ) : List Bool → List Bool :=
  BlockLoop.step (fun _ _ => [true])
    (fun _ r => pairEncode
      (if MultiTapeTM.indicator V (sliceTakeAt a k (pairSndD r)) then
        pairEncode (true :: pairFstD (pairFstD r)) (pairSndD (pairFstD r))
      else
        pairEncode (pairFstD (pairFstD r)) (true :: pairSndD (pairFstD r)))
      (sliceDropAt a k (pairSndD r)))

/-- The chunk function: at countdown exhaustion, emit one bit comparing the
two unary vote counters strictly (`uF < uT`). -/
private def majEmit : List Bool → List Bool :=
  BlockLoop.emit (fun s => [!decide ((pairFstD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s)))).length ≤
    (pairSndD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s)))).length)])

/-- The initial state: live marker, unary countdown `a'·(n+1)^k'`, empty vote
counters, and the normalized input pair. -/
private def majInit (a' k' : ℕ) (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode [true]
    (pairEncode (List.replicate (a' * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k') true)
      (pairEncode (pairEncode [] [])
        (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z))))

/-- The vote push grows the accumulator by at most four symbols. -/
private theorem length_majVote_le (b : Bool) (acc : List Bool) :
    (if b then pairEncode (true :: pairFstD acc) (pairSndD acc)
      else pairEncode (pairFstD acc) (true :: pairSndD acc)).length ≤ acc.length + 4 := by
  have hb := length_pair_components_le acc
  cases b with
  | true =>
    rw [if_pos rfl, length_pairEncode, List.length_cons]
    omega
  | false =>
    rw [if_neg (by simp), length_pairEncode, List.length_cons]
    omega

/-- The majority loop's machine-level output is the single aggregated bit.
**Proof sketch.** `Complexity.BlockLoop.loop_output` with the live marker as every head
and remainders `⟨⟨1^cT i, 1^(i - cT i)⟩, ⟨x, rem.drop (i·B)⟩⟩`, where `cT i` counts the
passing blocks among the first `i` (`List.countP_append` at `List.range_succ`): the vote
push adds the `i`-th block's vote and the block is dropped.  At exhaustion the emitted
comparison of the unary counters `¬(cT ≤ K - cT)` is the strict majority `K < 2·cT`, by
`decide_not` and arithmetic. -/
private theorem majLoop_output (V : Language Bool) (a k a' k' : ℕ) (z : List Bool) :
    (List.range (a' * ((majInit a' k' z).length + 1) ^ k' + 1)).flatMap
      (fun i => majEmit ((majStep V a k)^[i] (majInit a' k' z))) =
      [decide (a' * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k' <
        2 * (List.range (a' * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k')).countP
          (fun j => MultiTapeTM.indicator V
            (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z j))))] := by
  have hlen : (pairFstD z).length ≤ (majInit a' k' z).length := by
    simp only [majInit, length_pairEncode, List.length_replicate, List.length_cons,
      List.length_nil]
    omega
  have hcT : ∀ i, (List.range i).countP (fun j =>
      MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z j))) ≤ i :=
    fun i => le_trans List.countP_le_length (by simp)
  refine (BlockLoop.loop_output (g := majStep V a k) rfl (fun _ => [true])
    (fun i => pairEncode
      (pairEncode
        (List.replicate ((List.range i).countP (fun j =>
          MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z j)))) true)
        (List.replicate (i - (List.range i).countP (fun j =>
          MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z j)))) true))
      (pairEncode (pairFstD z)
        ((pairSndD z).drop (i * (a * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k)))))
    (by simp [majInit]) (fun _ _ => by simp) (fun _ _ => rfl) (fun i _ => ?_)
    (BlockLoop.lt_polyBudget_of_le a' k' hlen)).trans ?_
  · simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, BlockLoop.sliceDropAt_pairEncode_drop,
      BlockLoop.sliceTakeAt_pairEncode_drop]
    have hcnt : (List.range (i + 1)).countP (fun j =>
        MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z j))) =
        (List.range i).countP (fun j =>
          MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z j))) +
        (if MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z i))
          then 1 else 0) := by
      rw [List.range_succ, List.countP_append]
      simp [List.countP_cons]
    have hle := hcT i
    cases hb : MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z)
        (((pairSndD z).drop (i * (a * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k))).take
          (a * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k))) with
    | true =>
      have hb' : MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z i))
          = true := hb
      have hcT1 : (List.range (i + 1)).countP (fun j =>
          MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z j))) =
          (List.range i).countP (fun j =>
            MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z j))) + 1 := by
        rw [hcnt, hb']
        simp
      rw [if_pos rfl, hcT1, List.replicate_succ,
        show i + 1 - ((List.range i).countP (fun j =>
          MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z j))) + 1) =
          i - (List.range i).countP (fun j =>
            MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z j)))
        from by omega]
    | false =>
      have hb' : MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z i))
          = false := hb
      have hcT0 : (List.range (i + 1)).countP (fun j =>
          MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z j))) =
          (List.range i).countP (fun j =>
            MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z j))) := by
        rw [hcnt, hb']
        simp
      rw [if_neg (by simp), hcT0,
        show i + 1 - (List.range i).countP (fun j =>
          MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z j))) =
          (i - (List.range i).countP (fun j =>
            MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z j)))) + 1
        from by omega, List.replicate_succ]
  · have hK := hcT (a' * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k')
    simp only [pairSndD_pairEncode, pairFstD_pairEncode, List.length_replicate]
    congr 1
    rw [← decide_not]
    exact decide_eq_decide.mpr (by omega)

/-- The strict-majority-aggregated block test of a polynomial-time one-bit
indicator is polynomial-time.

**Proof sketch.** `Complexity.BlockLoop.polyTimeComputable_countdown` for the countdown
block loop whose head is the live marker and whose remainder carries two unary vote
counters (passed and failed blocks); the vote push is an `ite` on the block's indicator;
at countdown exhaustion the emitted bit is the strict comparison of their lengths
(`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_lenLe` after a `pairSwap`), which equals
`a'·(n+1)^k' < 2·(passed votes)` since the counts sum to the round total.  The vote push
grows the counters by at most four symbols (`length_majVote_le`), well within the
slack `16`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_blockMajorityTest {V : Language Bool}
    (hV : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [MultiTapeTM.indicator V z]))
    (a k a' k' : ℕ) :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun z =>
      [decide (a' * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k' <
        2 * (List.range (a' * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k')).countP
          (fun i => MultiTapeTM.indicator V
            (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z i))))]) := by
  have hzz : PolyTimeComputable (fun s => pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD s))) :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp
      (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  have hacc : PolyTimeComputable (fun s => pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s))) :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp
      (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  -- the vote push: an `ite` on the block's indicator over the two `true ::` prepends
  have hind : PolyTimeComputable (fun s =>
      [MultiTapeTM.indicator V (sliceTakeAt a k (pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD s))))]) :=
    hV.comp ((polyTimeComputable_sliceTakeAt a k).comp hzz)
  have huT : PolyTimeComputable (fun s =>
      pairFstD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s)))) :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp hacc
  have huF : PolyTimeComputable (fun s =>
      pairSndD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s)))) :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp hacc
  have hvote : PolyTimeComputable (fun s =>
      if MultiTapeTM.indicator V
          (sliceTakeAt a k (pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD s)))) then
        pairEncode (true :: pairFstD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s))))
          (pairSndD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s))))
      else
        pairEncode (pairFstD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s))))
          (true :: pairSndD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s))))) :=
    polyTimeComputable_ite hind (((polyTimeComputable_prepend [true]).comp huT).pairEncode huF)
      (huT.pairEncode ((polyTimeComputable_prepend [true]).comp huF))
  -- the emitted bit: the negated length test on the swapped counters
  have hle : PolyTimeComputable (fun s =>
      [decide ((pairFstD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s)))).length ≤
        (pairSndD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s)))).length)]) := by
    have h := polyTimeComputable_lenLe.comp (huF.pairEncode huT)
    have heq : (fun s =>
        [decide ((pairFstD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s)))).length ≤
          (pairSndD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s)))).length)]) =
        ((fun z => [decide ((pairSndD z).length ≤ (pairFstD z).length)]) ∘
          (fun s => pairEncode (pairSndD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s))))
            (pairFstD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD s)))))) := by
      funext s
      simp [Function.comp]
    rw [heq]
    exact h
  exact BlockLoop.polyTimeComputable_countdown (g := majStep V a k) (e := majEmit) rfl rfl
    [true] a' k' 16 (polyTimeComputable_const [true])
    (hvote.pairEncode ((polyTimeComputable_sliceDropAt a k).comp hzz))
    (polyTimeComputable_not hle) polyTimeComputable_pairFstD
    ((polyTimeComputable_const (pairEncode [] [])).pairEncode
      (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode polyTimeComputable_pairSndD))
    (fun f r _ => by
      have hpush := length_majVote_le
        (MultiTapeTM.indicator V (sliceTakeAt a k (pairSndD r))) (pairFstD r)
      have hslice := length_sliceDropAt_le a k (pairSndD r)
      have hY := length_pair_components_le r
      simp only [length_pairEncode, List.length_cons, List.length_nil]
      omega)
    (majLoop_output V a k a' k')

end Complexity
```


## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/ClassNP/PClosure.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.CoNP
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimePairing
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimeBlockMajority

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Closure properties of `P`

The class `P` [AB09, Def 1.13] is closed under polynomial-time preimages (many-one
reductions), under the Boolean operations, and hence under Boolean functions of finitely
many tests. These facts are used tacitly throughout [AB09] (e.g. ch. 2, ch. 5, ch. 6); here
they are derived from the function class FP (`TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimePairing`)
and the closure under complement (`Complexity.compl_mem_P`, `ClassNP/CoNP.lean`).

## Main definitions

None — this module only proves theorems about existing definitions.

## Main results

* `Complexity.mem_P_iff_polyTimeComputable` — `V ∈ P` iff its one-bit indicator is in FP;
  `Complexity.mem_P_of_test`, `Complexity.test_of_mem_P` — the same for Boolean tests.
* `Complexity.preimage_mem_P` — `P` is closed under polynomial-time preimages.
* `Complexity.inter_mem_P`, `Complexity.union_mem_P`, `Complexity.empty_mem_P`,
  `Complexity.univ_mem_P` — Boolean closure.
* `Complexity.mem_P_of_atoms` — `P` is closed under Boolean functions of finitely many
  tests.
* `Complexity.lenEq_mem_P`, `lenLe_mem_P`, `lenEq_preimage_mem_P`, `lenLe_preimage_mem_P`
  — length comparisons are in `P`.
* `Complexity.mem_P_of_blockAny`, `Complexity.mem_P_of_blockMajority`,
  `Complexity.mem_P_of_blockXorAny` — `P` is closed under running a `P`-decider on
  polynomially many polynomial-length blocks of the input and aggregating the answers
  (OR / strict majority / XOR-then-OR), the folklore repetition closures used tacitly
  by [AB09] ch. 7 (Theorems 7.8, 7.10, 7.14, 7.15); the machine engine is
  `TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimeBlockLoop`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.6, Definition 1.13; §2.2.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-! ### `P` and polynomial-time functions -/

/-- `V ∈ P` iff its singleton indicator `x ↦ [1_V(x)]` is polynomial-time computable. -/
theorem mem_P_iff_polyTimeComputable {V : Language Bool} :
    V ∈ P ↔ PolyTimeComputable (fun x => [MultiTapeTM.indicator V x]) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨C, c, M, hM⟩ := mem_P_iff.mp h
    exact ⟨M, C, c, hM⟩
  · rintro ⟨M, C, c, hM⟩
    exact mem_P_iff.mpr ⟨C, c, M, hM⟩

/-- **`P` is closed under polynomial-time preimages**: if `V ∈ P` and `g` is
polynomial-time computable then `g⁻¹(V) ∈ P` (the decider of `V` run on `g x`). -/
theorem preimage_mem_P {V : Language Bool} {g : List Bool → List Bool} (hV : V ∈ P)
    (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) : g ⁻¹' V ∈ P :=
  mem_P_iff_polyTimeComputable.mpr ((mem_P_iff_polyTimeComputable.mp hV).comp hg)

/-- A language whose Boolean test is polynomial-time computable (as a one-bit output) is
in `P`. -/
theorem mem_P_of_test {b : List Bool → Bool} (h : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [b z])) :
    {z | b z = true} ∈ P := by
  rw [mem_P_iff_polyTimeComputable]
  convert h using 2 with z
  by_cases hz : b z = true <;> simp [MultiTapeTM.indicator, hz]

/-- The Boolean test of a language in `P` is polynomial-time computable. -/
theorem test_of_mem_P {L : Language Bool} (h : L ∈ P) :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [MultiTapeTM.indicator L z]) :=
  mem_P_iff_polyTimeComputable.mp h

/-! ### Boolean closure -/

/-- **`P` is closed under intersection.** -/
theorem inter_mem_P {L₁ L₂ : Language Bool} (h₁ : L₁ ∈ P) (h₂ : L₂ ∈ P) :
    {z | z ∈ L₁ ∧ z ∈ L₂} ∈ P := by
  have h := mem_P_of_test (polyTimeComputable_and (test_of_mem_P h₁) (test_of_mem_P h₂))
  convert h using 1
  ext z
  by_cases a : z ∈ L₁ <;> by_cases b : z ∈ L₂ <;> simp [MultiTapeTM.indicator, a, b]

/-- **`P` is closed under union** (branching on the first test). -/
theorem union_mem_P {L₁ L₂ : Language Bool} (h₁ : L₁ ∈ P) (h₂ : L₂ ∈ P) :
    {z | z ∈ L₁ ∨ z ∈ L₂} ∈ P := by
  have ht : PolyTimeComputable
      (fun z => [MultiTapeTM.indicator L₁ z || MultiTapeTM.indicator L₂ z]) := by
    convert polyTimeComputable_ite (test_of_mem_P h₁) (polyTimeComputable_const [true])
      (test_of_mem_P h₂) using 1
    funext z
    cases MultiTapeTM.indicator L₁ z <;> rfl
  convert mem_P_of_test ht using 1
  ext z
  by_cases a : z ∈ L₁ <;> by_cases b : z ∈ L₂ <;> simp [MultiTapeTM.indicator, a, b]

/-- The empty language is in `P`. -/
theorem empty_mem_P : ({_z | false = true} : Language Bool) ∈ P :=
  mem_P_of_test (polyTimeComputable_const [false])

/-- The full language is in `P`. -/
theorem univ_mem_P : ({_z | true = true} : Language Bool) ∈ P :=
  mem_P_of_test (polyTimeComputable_const [true])

/-- **`P` is closed under Boolean functions of finitely many tests**: if each test
`b i` decides a language in `P`, so does `z ↦ F (b · z)` for any `F`.

**Proof sketch.** The language is the finite union, over the valuations `β` with
`F β = true`, of the finite intersections `⋂ᵢ {z | b i z = β i}`; each set in the
intersection is a test language or its complement. -/
theorem mem_P_of_atoms {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (b : ι → List Bool → Bool)
    (hb : ∀ i, ({z | b i z = true} : Language Bool) ∈ P) (F : (ι → Bool) → Bool) :
    ({z | F (fun i => b i z) = true} : Language Bool) ∈ P := by
  classical
  -- one valuation
  have hval : ∀ β : ι → Bool, ∀ s : Finset ι,
      ({z | ∀ i ∈ s, b i z = β i} : Language Bool) ∈ P := by
    intro β s
    induction s using Finset.induction_on with
    | empty => simpa using univ_mem_P
    | insert i s hi ih =>
      have hi' : ({z | b i z = β i} : Language Bool) ∈ P := by
        cases hβ : β i
        · have := compl_mem_P (hb i)
          convert this using 1
          ext z
          change b i z = false ↔ ¬ (b i z = true)
          simp
        · exact hb i
      have := inter_mem_P hi' ih
      convert this using 1
      ext z
      simp
  have hunion : ∀ s : Finset (ι → Bool),
      ({z | ∃ β ∈ s, ∀ i, b i z = β i} : Language Bool) ∈ P := by
    intro s
    induction s using Finset.induction_on with
    | empty => simpa using empty_mem_P
    | insert β s hβ ih =>
      have h1 := hval β Finset.univ
      have := union_mem_P h1 ih
      convert this using 1
      ext z
      change (∃ β' ∈ insert β s, ∀ i, b i z = β' i) ↔
        (∀ i ∈ Finset.univ, b i z = β i) ∨ (∃ β' ∈ s, ∀ i, b i z = β' i)
      simp
  have h := hunion (Finset.univ.filter fun β => F β = true)
  convert h using 1
  ext z
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
  constructor
  · intro hz; exact ⟨_, hz, fun i => rfl⟩
  · rintro ⟨β, hβ, hb'⟩
    have : (fun i => b i z) = β := funext hb'
    rw [this]; exact hβ

/-! ### Length comparisons -/

/-- The words whose two components under the total default projections
(`pairFstD`/`pairSndD`, both `[]` on malformed input) have equal length form a language
in `P`. Malformed words project to `([], [])` and are therefore members — e.g. `[]`
itself; the well-formed-pair corollaries below are unaffected (P0 round 1, finding 5). -/
theorem lenEq_mem_P : {z : List Bool | (pairFstD z).length = (pairSndD z).length} ∈ P := by
  have h := mem_P_of_test polyTimeComputable_lenEq
  simpa using h

/-- The words whose second default-projected component is at most as long as the first
form a language in `P` — with the same totalization as `Complexity.lenEq_mem_P`:
malformed words project to `([], [])` and are members. -/
theorem lenLe_mem_P : {z : List Bool | (pairSndD z).length ≤ (pairFstD z).length} ∈ P := by
  have h := mem_P_of_test polyTimeComputable_lenLe
  simpa using h

/-- Comparing the lengths of two polynomial-time computable strings is in `P`. -/
theorem lenEq_preimage_mem_P {f g : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) : {z | (f z).length = (g z).length} ∈ P := by
  have h := preimage_mem_P lenEq_mem_P (hf.pairEncode hg)
  simpa using h

/-- `|g z| ≤ |f z|` for polynomial-time `f`, `g` is decidable in `P`. -/
theorem lenLe_preimage_mem_P {f g : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) : {z | (g z).length ≤ (f z).length} ∈ P := by
  have h := preimage_mem_P lenLe_mem_P (hf.pairEncode hg)
  simpa using h

/-! ### Block-query closure

`P` is closed under running a `P`-decider on polynomially many fixed-size blocks of
the second component of a pair and aggregating the answers.  `blockAt a k z i` is the
`i`-th length-`a·(n+1)^k` block of `pairSndD z`, with `n = |pairFstD z|`; the block
count is `a'·(n+1)^k'`.  These are the folklore "repeat the machine polynomially many
times" closures that [AB09] ch. 7 uses tacitly (§7.3, Theorem 7.8; §7.4.1;
Theorems 7.14–7.15); the machine-level loop lives in
`TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimeBlockLoop`.

Like the length comparisons above, all three languages are total extensions through
the default projections: a malformed word is classified by the same test on its
default-decoded components (for the nested pair, an invalid inner pair leaves only the
outer mask), and `V` is consulted only on re-encoded queries (ch7 fill audit, note 3). -/

/-- **`P` is closed under a polynomial block-OR**: if `V ∈ P` then so is the set of
pairs some of whose `a'·(n+1)^k'` blocks of length `a·(n+1)^k` passes `V`'s test,
paired with the first component. -/
theorem mem_P_of_blockAny {V : Language Bool} (hV : V ∈ P) (a k a' k' : ℕ) :
    {z : List Bool | ∃ i < a' * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k',
      pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z i) ∈ V} ∈ P := by
  have h := mem_P_of_test (polyTimeComputable_blockAnyTest (test_of_mem_P hV) a k a' k')
  convert h using 1
  ext z
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, List.any_eq_true, List.mem_range]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨i, hi, hmem⟩
    exact ⟨i, hi, by simp [MultiTapeTM.indicator, hmem]⟩
  · rintro ⟨i, hi, hbit⟩
    refine ⟨i, hi, ?_⟩
    by_contra hmem
    simp [MultiTapeTM.indicator, hmem] at hbit

/-- **`P` is closed under a polynomial block-majority**: if `V ∈ P` then so is the
set of pairs a strict majority of whose `a'·(n+1)^k'` blocks of length `a·(n+1)^k`
passes `V`'s test, paired with the first component. -/
theorem mem_P_of_blockMajority {V : Language Bool} (hV : V ∈ P) (a k a' k' : ℕ) :
    {z : List Bool | a' * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k' <
      2 * (List.range (a' * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k')).countP
        (fun i => MultiTapeTM.indicator V (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z i)))} ∈ P := by
  have h := mem_P_of_test (polyTimeComputable_blockMajorityTest (test_of_mem_P hV) a k a' k')
  convert h using 1
  ext z
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, decide_eq_true_eq]

/-- **`P` is closed under a polynomial XOR-shifted block-OR**: on a nested pair
`⟨⟨x, u⟩, v⟩`, if `V ∈ P` then so is the set of nested pairs some of whose
`a'·(|x|+1)^k'` blocks of `u` of length `a·(|x|+1)^k`, XORed bitwise with `v`
(truncating to the shorter word), passes `V`'s test paired with `x`. -/
theorem mem_P_of_blockXorAny {V : Language Bool} (hV : V ∈ P) (a k a' k' : ℕ) :
    {w : List Bool | ∃ i < a' * ((pairFstD (pairFstD w)).length + 1) ^ k',
      pairEncode (pairFstD (pairFstD w))
        (List.zipWith xor (pairSndD w) (blockAt a k (pairFstD w) i)) ∈ V} ∈ P := by
  have h := mem_P_of_test (polyTimeComputable_blockXorAnyTest (test_of_mem_P hV) a k a' k')
  convert h using 1
  ext w
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, List.any_eq_true, List.mem_range]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨i, hi, hmem⟩
    exact ⟨i, hi, by simp [MultiTapeTM.indicator, hmem]⟩
  · rintro ⟨i, hi, hbit⟩
    refine ⟨i, hi, ?_⟩
    by_contra hmem
    simp [MultiTapeTM.indicator, hmem] at hbit

end Complexity
```

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 The TCSlib Authors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib Contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.Basic
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PClosure

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Binary comparison, addition and subtraction in polynomial time

Infrastructure for [AB09 §7.2]; not itself a result of the book. A pair of numbers is the
word `pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)`; every operation is defined on all words, reading
the components with `Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal` (so malformed words count as `0`), and
outputs a normalized word `Nat.bits n` or a one-bit answer.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.BinArith.add`, `Complexity.BinArith.sub` — sum and truncated difference.
* `Complexity.BinArith.lt`, `Complexity.BinArith.le`, `Complexity.BinArith.beq` — comparisons.

## Main results

* `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_add`, `polyTimeComputable_sub` — the carry and
  borrow chains are one finite-state scan (`Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_serial`)
  followed by normalization.
* `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_lt`, `polyTimeComputable_le`,
  `polyTimeComputable_beq`, and the languages `lt_mem_P`, `le_mem_P`, `beq_mem_P`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§7.2.)
-/

namespace Complexity

namespace BinArith

open Turing LogProg

/-! ### Carry and borrow chains -/

/-- The carry out of a full adder with carry in `c` and bits `x`, `y`. -/
def carry (c x y : Bool) : Bool := (x && y) || (c && (x ^^ y))

/-- The sum (and difference) bit `x ⊕ y ⊕ c`. -/
def sumBit (c x y : Bool) : Bool := (x ^^ y) ^^ c

/-- The borrow out of a full subtractor computing `x - y - c`. -/
def borrow (c x y : Bool) : Bool := (!x && y) || (!(x ^^ y) && c)

/-- **The carry chain adds**: over `N` padded pairs of words of length at most `N`, the
output plus `2^N` times the final carry is `bitsVal a + bitsVal b + c`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `N`: a full-adder step satisfies `s + 2c' = x + y + c`, and
the scan of the tails accounts for the rest at weight `2`. -/
theorem serial_add : ∀ (N : ℕ) (a b : List Bool) (c : Bool), a.length ≤ N → b.length ≤ N →
    bitsVal (serialOut carry sumBit c (padZip a b N)) +
        2 ^ N * (serialState carry c (padZip a b N)).toNat =
      bitsVal a + bitsVal b + c.toNat := by
  intro N
  induction N with
  | zero =>
    intro a b c ha hb
    rw [List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by omega : a.length = 0),
      List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by omega : b.length = 0)]
    simp [padZip, serialOut, serialState, bitsVal]
  | succ N ih =>
    intro a b c ha hb
    have hbit : ∀ c x y : Bool,
        (sumBit c x y).toNat + 2 * (carry c x y).toNat = x.toNat + y.toNat + c.toNat := by
      decide
    have h := ih (a.drop 1) (b.drop 1) (carry c (a.headD false) (b.headD false))
      (by simp; omega) (by simp; omega)
    have h2 := hbit c (a.headD false) (b.headD false)
    rw [bitsVal_eq_headD a, bitsVal_eq_headD b]
    simp only [padZip, serialOut, serialState, bitsVal, pow_succ]
    linarith

/-- **The borrow chain subtracts**: over `N` padded pairs of words of length at most `N`, the
output plus `bitsVal b + c` is `bitsVal a` plus `2^N` times the final borrow.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `N`: a full-subtractor step satisfies `d + y + c = x + 2c'`. -/
theorem serial_sub : ∀ (N : ℕ) (a b : List Bool) (c : Bool), a.length ≤ N → b.length ≤ N →
    bitsVal (serialOut borrow sumBit c (padZip a b N)) + bitsVal b + c.toNat =
      bitsVal a + 2 ^ N * (serialState borrow c (padZip a b N)).toNat := by
  intro N
  induction N with
  | zero =>
    intro a b c ha hb
    rw [List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by omega : a.length = 0),
      List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by omega : b.length = 0)]
    cases c <;> simp [padZip, serialOut, serialState, bitsVal]
  | succ N ih =>
    intro a b c ha hb
    have hbit : ∀ c x y : Bool,
        (sumBit c x y).toNat + y.toNat + c.toNat = x.toNat + 2 * (borrow c x y).toNat := by
      decide
    have h := ih (a.drop 1) (b.drop 1) (borrow c (a.headD false) (b.headD false))
      (by simp; omega) (by simp; omega)
    have h2 := hbit c (a.headD false) (b.headD false)
    rw [bitsVal_eq_headD a, bitsVal_eq_headD b]
    simp only [padZip, serialOut, serialState, bitsVal, pow_succ]
    linarith

/-- Both component values of `z` are below `2^(|z|+2)`, the scan length used on `z`. -/
private theorem serial_bounds (z : List Bool) :
    bitsVal (pairFstD z) < 2 ^ (z.length + 2) ∧ bitsVal (pairSndD z) < 2 ^ (z.length + 2) := by
  have h1 := (bitsVal_lt_two_pow (pairFstD z)).trans_le
    (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) ((length_pairFstD_le z).trans (Nat.le_add_right _ 2)))
  have h2 := (bitsVal_lt_two_pow (pairSndD z)).trans_le
    (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) ((length_pairSndD_le z).trans (Nat.le_add_right _ 2)))
  exact ⟨h1, h2⟩

/-- On a word `z`, the final borrow of the subtraction scan decides `fst < snd`, and when it
is clear the scan's output is the difference. -/
theorem serial_sub_spec (z : List Bool) :
    serialState borrow false (padZip (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) (z.length + 2)) =
        decide (bitsVal (pairFstD z) < bitsVal (pairSndD z)) ∧
      (bitsVal (pairSndD z) ≤ bitsVal (pairFstD z) →
        bitsVal (serialOut borrow sumBit false (padZip (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) (z.length + 2)))
          = bitsVal (pairFstD z) - bitsVal (pairSndD z)) := by
  have h := serial_sub (z.length + 2) (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) false
    (by have := length_pairFstD_le z; omega) (by have := length_pairSndD_le z; omega)
  have hR := bitsVal_lt_two_pow
    (serialOut borrow sumBit false (padZip (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) (z.length + 2)))
  rw [length_serialOut, length_padZip] at hR
  obtain ⟨ha, hb⟩ := serial_bounds z
  generalize 2 ^ (z.length + 2) = P at h hR ha hb
  cases hs : serialState borrow false (padZip (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) (z.length + 2)) <;>
    simp only [hs, Bool.toNat_false, Bool.toNat_true] at h <;> simp at h ⊢ <;> omega

/-! ### Addition and subtraction -/

/-- The sum of the values of the two components of `z`, as a binary word. -/
def add (z : List Bool) : List Bool := Nat.bits (bitsVal (pairFstD z) + bitsVal (pairSndD z))

/-- The truncated difference `fst ∸ snd` of the values of the components of `z`. -/
def sub (z : List Bool) : List Bool := Nat.bits (bitsVal (pairFstD z) - bitsVal (pairSndD z))

/-- `add` on encoded numbers is addition. -/
@[simp] theorem add_pairEncode (a b : ℕ) :
    add (pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)) = Nat.bits (a + b) := by
  simp [add, bitsVal_bits]

/-- `sub` on encoded numbers is truncated subtraction. -/
@[simp] theorem sub_pairEncode (a b : ℕ) :
    sub (pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)) = Nat.bits (a - b) := by
  simp [sub, bitsVal_bits]

/-- **Binary addition is polynomial-time** (infrastructure for [AB09 §7.2]; not itself a
result of the book): the carry chain, then normalization.

**Proof sketch.** Scan `|z| + 2` padded pairs (`serial_add`); since `a + b < 2^{|z|+2}` the
final carry is `0`, so the output has value `a + b`, and `polyTimeComputable_normBits`
normalizes it. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_add : PolyTimeComputable add := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_normBits.comp (polyTimeComputable_serial carry sumBit false) using 1
  funext z
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, add]
  congr 1
  have h := serial_add (z.length + 2) (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) false
    (by have := length_pairFstD_le z; omega) (by have := length_pairSndD_le z; omega)
  have hlt : bitsVal (pairFstD z) + bitsVal (pairSndD z) < 2 ^ (z.length + 2) := by
    have h1 := (bitsVal_lt_two_pow (pairFstD z)).trans_le
      (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (length_pairFstD_le z))
    have h2 := (bitsVal_lt_two_pow (pairSndD z)).trans_le
      (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (length_pairSndD_le z))
    have : 2 ^ (z.length + 2) = 4 * 2 ^ z.length := by ring
    omega
  generalize 2 ^ (z.length + 2) = P at h hlt
  cases hs : serialState carry false (padZip (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) (z.length + 2)) <;>
    simp only [hs, Bool.toNat_false, Bool.toNat_true] at h <;> omega

/-! ### Comparisons -/

/-- The test `fst < snd` on the values of the components of `z`. -/
def lt (z : List Bool) : Bool := decide (bitsVal (pairFstD z) < bitsVal (pairSndD z))

/-- The test `fst ≤ snd` on the values of the components of `z`. -/
def le (z : List Bool) : Bool := decide (bitsVal (pairFstD z) ≤ bitsVal (pairSndD z))

/-- The test `fst = snd` on the values of the components of `z`. -/
def beq (z : List Bool) : Bool := decide (bitsVal (pairFstD z) = bitsVal (pairSndD z))

/-- `lt` on encoded numbers is `<`. -/
@[simp] theorem lt_pairEncode (a b : ℕ) :
    lt (pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)) = decide (a < b) := by simp [lt, bitsVal_bits]

/-- `le` on encoded numbers is `≤`. -/
@[simp] theorem le_pairEncode (a b : ℕ) :
    le (pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)) = decide (a ≤ b) := by simp [le, bitsVal_bits]

/-- `beq` on encoded numbers is `=`. -/
@[simp] theorem beq_pairEncode (a b : ℕ) :
    beq (pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)) = decide (a = b) := by simp [beq, bitsVal_bits]

/-- **Binary comparison `<` is polynomial-time**: the last bit of the scan emitting the
running borrow is the final borrow. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_lt : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [lt z]) := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_lastBit.comp (polyTimeComputable_serial borrow borrow false) using 1
  funext z
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, lt]
  rw [getLastD_serialOut_self _ _ _ (by
    rw [← List.length_pos_iff, length_padZip]; omega), (serial_sub_spec z).1]

/-- **Binary comparison `≤` is polynomial-time** (`¬ snd < fst`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_le : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [le z]) := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_not (polyTimeComputable_lt.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSwap)
    using 1
  funext z
  by_cases h : bitsVal (pairSndD z) < bitsVal (pairFstD z) <;> simp [h, le, lt]
  omega

/-- **Binary equality is polynomial-time** (`≤` both ways). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_beq : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [beq z]) := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_and polyTimeComputable_le
    (polyTimeComputable_le.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSwap) using 1
  funext z
  simp only [le, beq, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode,
    List.cons.injEq, and_true]
  by_cases h : bitsVal (pairFstD z) = bitsVal (pairSndD z)
  · simp [h]
  · rcases Nat.lt_or_gt_of_ne h with h' | h' <;> simp [h, h'.le, Nat.not_le_of_lt h']

/-- **Binary subtraction is polynomial-time**: `0` when `fst < snd`, else the borrow chain's
output, normalized. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_sub : PolyTimeComputable sub := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_ite polyTimeComputable_lt (polyTimeComputable_const [])
    (polyTimeComputable_normBits.comp (polyTimeComputable_serial borrow sumBit false)) using 1
  funext z
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, sub, lt]
  by_cases h : bitsVal (pairFstD z) < bitsVal (pairSndD z)
  · simp [h, Nat.sub_eq_zero_of_le h.le, Nat.zero_bits]
  · simp only [h, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false]
    rw [(serial_sub_spec z).2 (by omega)]

/-- The language `{⟨a, b⟩ : a < b}` is in `P` (components read by `bitsVal`; malformed words
read as 0). -/
theorem lt_mem_P : {z | lt z = true} ∈ P := mem_P_of_test polyTimeComputable_lt

/-- The language `{⟨a, b⟩ : a ≤ b}` is in `P` (components read by `bitsVal`; malformed words
read as 0). -/
theorem le_mem_P : {z | le z = true} ∈ P := mem_P_of_test polyTimeComputable_le

/-- The language `{⟨a, b⟩ : a = b}` is in `P` (components read by `bitsVal`; malformed words
read as 0). -/
theorem beq_mem_P : {z | beq z = true} ∈ P := mem_P_of_test polyTimeComputable_beq

end BinArith

end Complexity
```


## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/ClassP/BinaryArith/Mul.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 The TCSlib Authors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib Contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.AddSub

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Binary multiplication and word reversal in polynomial time

Infrastructure for [AB09 §7.2]; not itself a result of the book. Multiplication is the
shift-and-add loop, run through `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_iterate`; reversal
(used by long division, which reads the dividend from its top bit) is the same kind of loop.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.BinArith.mul` — the product of the two components of a pair.
* `Complexity.BinArith.mulStep` — one round of shift-and-add on `⟨A, ⟨B, acc⟩⟩`.
* `Complexity.BinArith.revStep` — one round of reversal on `⟨src, acc⟩`.

## Main results

* `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_mul` — binary multiplication is polynomial-time.
* `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_reverse` — word reversal is polynomial-time.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§7.2.)
-/

namespace Complexity

namespace BinArith

open Turing LogProg

/-! ### Reversal -/

/-- One round of reversal on `⟨src, acc⟩`: move the head of `src` onto `acc`. -/
def revStep (S : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if isNilB (pairFstD S) then S
  else pairEncode ((pairFstD S).drop 1) ((pairFstD S).headD false :: pairSndD S)

/-- A reversal round is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_revStep : PolyTimeComputable revStep := by
  unfold revStep
  refine polyTimeComputable_ite (polyTimeComputable_isNil.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD)
    polyTimeComputable_id ?_
  exact (polyTimeComputable_tail.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD).pairEncode
    (polyTimeComputable_cons (polyTimeComputable_headD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD)
      polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)

/-- Reversal rounds keep `reverse src ++ acc` and the total length. -/
theorem revStep_pairEncode (u v : List Bool) :
    ∃ u' v', revStep (pairEncode u v) = pairEncode u' v' ∧ u'.reverse ++ v' = u.reverse ++ v ∧
      u'.length + v'.length = u.length + v.length ∧ (u ≠ [] → u'.length < u.length) ∧
      (u = [] → u' = []) := by
  cases u with
  | nil => exact ⟨[], v, by simp [revStep, isNilB], rfl, rfl, by simp, fun _ => rfl⟩
  | cons b u =>
    refine ⟨u, b :: v, by simp [revStep, isNilB], by simp, by simp; omega, by simp, by simp⟩

/-- **Word reversal is polynomial-time**: `|w| + 1` reversal rounds from `⟨w, []⟩`.

**Proof sketch.** Each round moves the head of `src` onto `acc`, keeping
`reverse src ++ acc = reverse w` and the total length; `|src|` reaches `0` within `|w|`
rounds, after which the state is fixed and `acc = reverse w`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_reverse : PolyTimeComputable (fun w : List Bool => w.reverse) := by
  let I : List Bool → List Bool → Prop := fun w S => ∃ u v, S = pairEncode u v ∧
    u.reverse ++ v = w.reverse ∧ u.length + v.length = w.length
  have hI : ∀ w S, I w S → I w (revStep S) := by
    rintro w S ⟨u, v, rfl, h1, h2⟩
    obtain ⟨u', v', he, h1', h2', -, -⟩ := revStep_pairEncode u v
    exact ⟨u', v', he, h1'.trans h1, h2'.trans h2⟩
  have h0 : ∀ w, I w (pairEncode w []) := fun w => ⟨w, [], rfl, by simp, by simp⟩
  have hinit : PolyTimeComputable (fun w : List Bool => pairEncode w []) :=
    polyTimeComputable_id.pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_const [])
  have hloop := polyTimeComputable_iterate polyTimeComputable_revStep hinit 1 1 3 1
    (fun w i _ => by
      obtain ⟨u, v, he, -, h2⟩ := iterate_invariant (I w) (hI w) i (h0 w)
      rw [he, length_pairEncode]; simp; omega)
  convert polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp hloop using 1
  funext w
  obtain ⟨u, v, he, h1, -⟩ := iterate_invariant (I w) (hI w) (1 * (w.length + 1) ^ 1) (h0 w)
  have hμ := iterate_measure_eq_zero (g := revStep) (I w) (fun S => (pairFstD S).length) (hI w)
    (by
      rintro S ⟨u, v, rfl, -, -⟩ hpos
      obtain ⟨u', v', he', -, -, hlt, -⟩ := revStep_pairEncode u v
      rw [he']; simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode] at hpos ⊢
      exact hlt (List.ne_nil_of_length_pos hpos))
    (by
      rintro S ⟨u, v, rfl, -, -⟩ h0
      simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, List.length_eq_zero_iff] at h0
      subst h0; simp [revStep, isNilB])
    (1 * (w.length + 1) ^ 1) (pairEncode w []) (h0 w) (by simp)
  rw [he] at hμ
  simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, List.length_eq_zero_iff] at hμ
  subst hμ
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, he, pairSndD_pairEncode]
  simpa using h1.symm

/-! ### Multiplication -/

/-- The product of the values of the two components of `z`, as a binary word. -/
def mul (z : List Bool) : List Bool := Nat.bits (bitsVal (pairFstD z) * bitsVal (pairSndD z))

/-- `mul` on encoded numbers is multiplication. -/
@[simp] theorem mul_pairEncode (a b : ℕ) :
    mul (pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)) = Nat.bits (a * b) := by
  simp [mul, bitsVal_bits]

/-- One round of shift-and-add on `⟨A, ⟨B, acc⟩⟩`: if the low bit of `B` is set add `A` to
`acc`; then double `A` and halve `B`. A state with `B = []` is fixed. -/
def mulStep (S : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if isNilB (pairFstD (pairSndD S)) then S
  else pairEncode (false :: pairFstD S)
    (pairEncode ((pairFstD (pairSndD S)).drop 1)
      (if (pairFstD (pairSndD S)).headD false then
        add (pairEncode (pairSndD (pairSndD S)) (pairFstD S))
      else pairSndD (pairSndD S)))

/-- A shift-and-add round is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_mulStep : PolyTimeComputable mulStep := by
  unfold mulStep
  refine polyTimeComputable_ite (polyTimeComputable_isNil.comp polyTimeComputable_slot2)
    polyTimeComputable_id ?_
  refine (polyTimeComputable_cons (polyTimeComputable_const [false])
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD).pairEncode
    ((polyTimeComputable_tail.comp polyTimeComputable_slot2).pairEncode ?_)
  exact polyTimeComputable_ite (polyTimeComputable_headD.comp polyTimeComputable_slot2)
    (polyTimeComputable_add.comp (polyTimeComputable_slot3.pairEncode polyTimeComputable_pairFstD))
    polyTimeComputable_slot3

/-- The invariant of the multiplication loop on input `z`: `acc + A·B = a·b`, `acc` is
normalized, and `|A| + |B|` does not grow. -/
def MulInv (z S : List Bool) : Prop :=
  ∃ A B C, S = pairEncode A (pairEncode B C) ∧
    bitsVal C + bitsVal A * bitsVal B = bitsVal (pairFstD z) * bitsVal (pairSndD z) ∧
    C = Nat.bits (bitsVal C) ∧ A.length + B.length ≤ (pairFstD z).length + (pairSndD z).length

/-- The shift-and-add round preserves the invariant, and shortens a nonempty `B`.

**Proof sketch.** With `B = b₀ + 2B'`, the round maps `acc + A·B` to `(acc + b₀A) + 2A·B'`,
the same value; `|A|` grows by one while `|B|` drops by one. -/
theorem mulInv_step {z S : List Bool} (h : MulInv z S) :
    MulInv z (mulStep S) ∧
      ((pairFstD (pairSndD S)) ≠ [] →
        (pairFstD (pairSndD (mulStep S))).length < (pairFstD (pairSndD S)).length) ∧
      ((pairFstD (pairSndD S)) = [] → mulStep S = S) := by
  obtain ⟨A, B, C, rfl, hv, hC, hl⟩ := h
  have hB := bitsVal_eq_headD B
  simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode]
  refine ⟨?_, fun hne => ?_, fun he => by simp [mulStep, isNilB, he]⟩
  · unfold mulStep
    simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode]
    split_ifs with h1 h2
    · exact ⟨A, B, C, rfl, hv, hC, hl⟩
    · have hne : B ≠ [] := by simpa [isNilB] using h1
      refine ⟨false :: A, B.drop 1, _, rfl, ?_, by simp [add, bitsVal_bits], ?_⟩
      · simp only [add, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, bitsVal_bits, bitsVal,
          Bool.toNat_false, zero_add]
        rw [h2, Bool.toNat_true] at hB
        rw [← hv, hB]; ring
      · have := List.length_pos_iff.mpr hne
        simp; omega
    · have hne : B ≠ [] := by simpa [isNilB] using h1
      refine ⟨false :: A, B.drop 1, C, rfl, ?_, hC, ?_⟩
      · simp only [bitsVal, Bool.toNat_false, zero_add]
        simp only [Bool.not_eq_true] at h2
        rw [h2, Bool.toNat_false, zero_add] at hB
        rw [← hv, hB]; ring
      · have := List.length_pos_iff.mpr hne
        simp; omega
  · have hne' : isNilB B = false := by simpa [isNilB] using hne
    simp only [mulStep, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, hne', Bool.false_eq_true,
      if_false, List.length_drop]
    have := List.length_pos_iff.mpr hne
    omega

/-- A state satisfying the multiplication invariant has length at most `4(|z| + 1)`
(`acc ≤ a·b < 2^{|a|+|b|}` bounds the normalized `acc`). -/
theorem length_le_of_mulInv {z S : List Bool} (h : MulInv z S) : S.length ≤ 4 * (z.length + 1) := by
  obtain ⟨A, B, C, rfl, hv, hC, hl⟩ := h
  have hCl : C.length ≤ (pairFstD z).length + (pairSndD z).length := by
    rw [hC]
    apply length_bits_le
    calc bitsVal C ≤ bitsVal (pairFstD z) * bitsVal (pairSndD z) := by omega
      _ < 2 ^ (pairFstD z).length * 2 ^ (pairSndD z).length := by
          rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (bitsVal (pairSndD z)) with h0 | h0
          · rw [h0, mul_zero]; positivity
          · exact Nat.mul_lt_mul_of_lt_of_le (bitsVal_lt_two_pow _)
              (bitsVal_lt_two_pow _).le (by positivity)
      _ = 2 ^ ((pairFstD z).length + (pairSndD z).length) := by rw [pow_add]
  have hz := length_pair_components_le z
  simp only [length_pairEncode]
  omega

/-- The input state `⟨a, ⟨b, []⟩⟩` of the multiplication loop. -/
def mulInit (z : List Bool) : List Bool := pairEncode (pairFstD z) (pairEncode (pairSndD z) [])

/-- The input state satisfies the multiplication invariant. -/
theorem mulInv_init (z : List Bool) : MulInv z (mulInit z) :=
  ⟨_, _, [], rfl, by simp [bitsVal], by simp [bitsVal, Nat.zero_bits], le_rfl⟩

/-- **Binary multiplication is polynomial-time** (infrastructure for [AB09 §7.2]; not
itself a result of the book).

**Proof sketch.** Run `|z| + 1` shift-and-add rounds from `⟨a, ⟨b, []⟩⟩`
(`polyTimeComputable_iterate`). The invariant `acc + A·B = a·b` (`MulInv`) holds throughout
and bounds the state length linearly; `|B|` drops each round until `B = []`, which is then
fixed (`iterate_measure_eq_zero`), so the final `acc` is `Nat.bits (a·b)`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_mul : PolyTimeComputable mul := by
  have hinit : PolyTimeComputable mulInit :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode
      (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_const []))
  have hloop := polyTimeComputable_iterate polyTimeComputable_mulStep hinit 1 1 4 1
    (fun z i _ => by
      simpa using length_le_of_mulInv
        (iterate_invariant (MulInv z) (fun _ h => (mulInv_step h).1) i (mulInv_init z)))
  convert polyTimeComputable_slot3.comp hloop using 1
  funext z
  have hμ := iterate_measure_eq_zero (g := mulStep) (MulInv z)
    (fun S => (pairFstD (pairSndD S)).length) (fun _ h => (mulInv_step h).1)
    (fun S h hpos => (mulInv_step h).2.1 (List.ne_nil_of_length_pos hpos))
    (fun S h h0 => (mulInv_step h).2.2 (List.length_eq_zero_iff.mp h0))
    (1 * (z.length + 1) ^ 1) (mulInit z) (mulInv_init z)
    (by simp [mulInit]; have := length_pairSndD_le z; omega)
  obtain ⟨A, B, C, he, hv, hC, -⟩ :=
    iterate_invariant (MulInv z) (fun _ h => (mulInv_step h).1) (1 * (z.length + 1) ^ 1)
      (mulInv_init z)
  rw [he] at hμ
  simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, List.length_eq_zero_iff] at hμ
  subst hμ
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, he, pairSndD_pairEncode, mul]
  rw [hC]
  simp only [bitsVal, mul_zero, add_zero] at hv
  rw [hv]

end BinArith

end Complexity
```

```text
/-
```
