```text
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib Contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.Mul

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Binary division with remainder in polynomial time

Infrastructure for [AB09 §7.2]; not itself a result of the book. Schoolbook long division:
the dividend is reversed (top bit first) and consumed one bit per round of
`Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_iterate`, shifting it into a running remainder from
which the divisor is subtracted whenever it fits. Division by `0` follows Lean's convention
(`a / 0 = 0`, `a % 0 = a`).

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.BinArith.div`, `Complexity.BinArith.mod` — quotient and remainder of the two
  components of a pair.
* `Complexity.BinArith.divStep` — one round of long division on `⟨b, ⟨R, ⟨r, q⟩⟩⟩`.

## Main results

* `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_isZero` — the zero test.
* `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_div`, `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_mod`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§7.2.)
-/

namespace Complexity

namespace BinArith

open Turing LogProg

/-- The zero test `bitsVal w = 0` is polynomial-time (no `1` in `w`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_isZero :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun w : List Bool => [decide (bitsVal w = 0)]) := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_not polyTimeComputable_any using 1
  funext w
  cases h : w.any id <;> simp [bitsVal_eq_zero_iff, h]

/-- The quotient of the values of the two components of `z`, as a binary word. -/
def div (z : List Bool) : List Bool := Nat.bits (bitsVal (pairFstD z) / bitsVal (pairSndD z))

/-- The remainder of the values of the two components of `z`, as a binary word. -/
def mod (z : List Bool) : List Bool := Nat.bits (bitsVal (pairFstD z) % bitsVal (pairSndD z))

/-- `div` on encoded numbers is `/`. -/
@[simp] theorem div_pairEncode (a b : ℕ) :
    div (pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)) = Nat.bits (a / b) := by simp [div, bitsVal_bits]

/-- `mod` on encoded numbers is `%`. -/
@[simp] theorem mod_pairEncode (a b : ℕ) :
    mod (pairEncode (Nat.bits a) (Nat.bits b)) = Nat.bits (a % b) := by simp [mod, bitsVal_bits]

/-- One round of long division on `⟨b, ⟨R, ⟨r, q⟩⟩⟩` (`R` the unread dividend, top bit
first): shift the next bit `c` into `r' = 2r + c`; if `b ≤ r'` subtract `b` and append a
quotient bit `1`, else append `0`. A state with `R = []` is fixed. -/
def divStep (S : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if isNilB (pairFstD (pairSndD S)) then S
  else if le (pairEncode (pairFstD S)
      ((pairFstD (pairSndD S)).headD false :: pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD S)))) then
    pairEncode (pairFstD S) (pairEncode ((pairFstD (pairSndD S)).drop 1)
      (pairEncode (sub (pairEncode ((pairFstD (pairSndD S)).headD false ::
        pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD S))) (pairFstD S)))
        (true :: pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD S)))))
  else
    pairEncode (pairFstD S) (pairEncode ((pairFstD (pairSndD S)).drop 1)
      (pairEncode ((pairFstD (pairSndD S)).headD false :: pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD S)))
        (false :: pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD S)))))

/-- A long-division round is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_divStep : PolyTimeComputable divStep := by
  have hs3 : PolyTimeComputable (fun S => pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD S))) :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp polyTimeComputable_slot3
  have hr' := polyTimeComputable_cons (polyTimeComputable_headD.comp polyTimeComputable_slot2) hs3
  have hR := polyTimeComputable_tail.comp polyTimeComputable_slot2
  unfold divStep
  refine polyTimeComputable_ite (polyTimeComputable_isNil.comp polyTimeComputable_slot2)
    polyTimeComputable_id ?_
  refine polyTimeComputable_ite (polyTimeComputable_le.comp
    (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode hr')) ?_ ?_
  · exact polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode (hR.pairEncode
      ((polyTimeComputable_sub.comp (hr'.pairEncode polyTimeComputable_pairFstD)).pairEncode
        (polyTimeComputable_cons (polyTimeComputable_const [true]) polyTimeComputable_slot4)))
  · exact polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode (hR.pairEncode (hr'.pairEncode
      (polyTimeComputable_cons (polyTimeComputable_const [false]) polyTimeComputable_slot4)))

/-- The input state `⟨b, ⟨reverse a, ⟨[], []⟩⟩⟩` of the division loop. -/
def divInit (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (pairSndD z) (pairEncode (pairFstD z).reverse (pairEncode [] []))

/-- The invariant of the division loop on input `z = ⟨a, b⟩`: the slots `r` and `q` grow by
at most one bit per consumed bit of `R`, and, when `b ≠ 0`, `(q·b + r)·2^|R| + R̄ = a` with
`r < b` (`R̄` the value of the unread bits). -/
def DivInv (z S : List Bool) : Prop :=
  ∃ R r q, S = pairEncode (pairSndD z) (pairEncode R (pairEncode r q)) ∧
    r.length + R.length ≤ (pairFstD z).length ∧ q.length + R.length ≤ (pairFstD z).length ∧
    (0 < bitsVal (pairSndD z) →
      (bitsVal q * bitsVal (pairSndD z) + bitsVal r) * 2 ^ R.length + bitsVal R.reverse =
        bitsVal (pairFstD z) ∧ bitsVal r < bitsVal (pairSndD z))

/-- The input state satisfies the division invariant. -/
theorem divInv_init (z : List Bool) : DivInv z (divInit z) :=
  ⟨_, [], [], rfl, by simp, by simp, fun _ => ⟨by simp [bitsVal], by simpa [bitsVal]⟩⟩

/-- The value step of a long-division round: from `(q·b + r)·2^(|R|+1) + R̄ c = a`, both the
subtracting and the non-subtracting round give the invariant for the shorter `R`. -/
private theorem div_value_step {Q ρ v c P T a : ℕ} (hc : c ≤ 1)
    (h : (Q * v + ρ) * (2 * P) + (T + c * P) = a) (hρ : ρ < v) :
    (v ≤ c + 2 * ρ → ((1 + 2 * Q) * v + (c + 2 * ρ - v)) * P + T = a ∧ c + 2 * ρ - v < v) ∧
    (¬ v ≤ c + 2 * ρ → ((2 * Q) * v + (c + 2 * ρ)) * P + T = a ∧ c + 2 * ρ < v) := by
  refine ⟨fun hle => ⟨?_, by omega⟩, fun hlt => ⟨?_, by omega⟩⟩
  · have : (1 + 2 * Q) * v + (c + 2 * ρ - v) = 2 * (Q * v + ρ) + c := by
      have := Nat.sub_add_cancel hle; nlinarith
    rw [this, ← h]; ring
  · rw [← h]; ring

/-- The long-division round preserves the invariant, and shortens a nonempty `R`.

**Proof sketch.** Consuming the next bit `c` of `R` turns `v = q·b + r` into `2v + c`; with
`r' = 2r + c < 2b`, subtracting `b` when it fits keeps `r < b` and sets the new quotient bit
(`div_value_step`). Each round removes one bit of `R` and adds at most one to `r` and `q`. -/
theorem divInv_step {z S : List Bool} (h : DivInv z S) :
    DivInv z (divStep S) ∧
      ((pairFstD (pairSndD S)) ≠ [] →
        (pairFstD (pairSndD (divStep S))).length < (pairFstD (pairSndD S)).length) ∧
      ((pairFstD (pairSndD S)) = [] → divStep S = S) := by
  obtain ⟨R, r, q, rfl, hl1, hl2, hv⟩ := h
  simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode]
  cases R with
  | nil => exact ⟨by simpa [divStep, isNilB] using ⟨[], r, q, rfl, hl1, hl2, hv⟩,
      by simp, fun _ => by simp [divStep, isNilB]⟩
  | cons c R =>
    refine ⟨?_, fun _ => ?_, by simp⟩
    swap
    · unfold divStep; split_ifs <;> simp_all [isNilB]
    have hc : c.toNat ≤ 1 := by cases c <;> simp
    have hrev : bitsVal (c :: R).reverse = bitsVal R.reverse + c.toNat * 2 ^ R.length := by
      rw [List.reverse_cons, bitsVal_append_singleton, List.length_reverse]
    have hr' : bitsVal (c :: r) = c.toNat + 2 * bitsVal r := rfl
    unfold divStep
    simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, isNilB, List.cons_ne_nil,
      decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, List.headD_cons, List.drop_succ_cons,
      List.drop_zero, le, sub]
    split_ifs with hle
    · refine ⟨R, _, true :: q, rfl, ?_, by simp at hl2 ⊢; omega, fun hb => ?_⟩
      · have := length_bits_le_of_le (c :: r) (n := bitsVal (c :: r) - bitsVal (pairSndD z))
          (Nat.sub_le _ _) le_rfl
        simp at hl1 this ⊢; omega
      · obtain ⟨hv1, hv2⟩ := hv hb
        rw [List.length_cons, pow_succ, hrev] at hv1
        have := (div_value_step (Q := bitsVal q) (ρ := bitsVal r)
          (P := 2 ^ R.length) (T := bitsVal R.reverse) (a := bitsVal (pairFstD z)) hc
          (by rw [← hv1]; ring) hv2).1 (by simpa [hr'] using hle)
        simp only [bitsVal_bits, bitsVal, Bool.toNat_true]
        exact this
    · refine ⟨R, _, false :: q, rfl, by simp at hl1 ⊢; omega, by simp at hl2 ⊢; omega,
        fun hb => ?_⟩
      obtain ⟨hv1, hv2⟩ := hv hb
      rw [List.length_cons, pow_succ, hrev] at hv1
      have := (div_value_step (Q := bitsVal q) (ρ := bitsVal r)
        (P := 2 ^ R.length) (T := bitsVal R.reverse) (a := bitsVal (pairFstD z)) hc
        (by rw [← hv1]; ring) hv2).2 (by simpa [hr'] using hle)
      simp only [bitsVal, Bool.toNat_false, zero_add]
      exact this

/-- A state satisfying the division invariant has length at most `7(|z| + 1)`. -/
theorem length_le_of_divInv {z S : List Bool} (h : DivInv z S) :
    S.length ≤ 7 * (z.length + 1) := by
  obtain ⟨R, r, q, rfl, hl1, hl2, -⟩ := h
  have hz := length_pair_components_le z
  simp only [length_pairEncode]
  omega

/-- The division loop: `|z| + 1` long-division rounds from `divInit z`. -/
def divLoop (z : List Bool) : List Bool := divStep^[1 * (z.length + 1) ^ 1] (divInit z)

/-- The division loop is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_divLoop : PolyTimeComputable divLoop := by
  have hinit : PolyTimeComputable divInit :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.pairEncode
      ((polyTimeComputable_reverse.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD).pairEncode
        (polyTimeComputable_const _))
  exact polyTimeComputable_iterate polyTimeComputable_divStep hinit 1 1 7 1 (fun z i _ => by
    simpa using length_le_of_divInv
      (iterate_invariant (DivInv z) (fun _ h => (divInv_step h).1) i (divInv_init z)))

/-- For a nonzero divisor the division loop ends with quotient slot `a / b` and remainder
slot `a % b` (by value).

**Proof sketch.** `|R|` drops each round (`iterate_measure_eq_zero`), so the final state has
`R = []`, where the invariant reads `q·b + r = a`, `r < b`; conclude by
`Nat.div_mod_unique`. -/
theorem divLoop_spec (z : List Bool) (hb : 0 < bitsVal (pairSndD z)) :
    bitsVal (pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD (divLoop z)))) =
        bitsVal (pairFstD z) / bitsVal (pairSndD z) ∧
      bitsVal (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD (divLoop z)))) =
        bitsVal (pairFstD z) % bitsVal (pairSndD z) := by
  have hμ := iterate_measure_eq_zero (g := divStep) (DivInv z)
    (fun S => (pairFstD (pairSndD S)).length) (fun _ h => (divInv_step h).1)
    (fun S h hpos => (divInv_step h).2.1 (List.ne_nil_of_length_pos hpos))
    (fun S h h0 => (divInv_step h).2.2 (List.length_eq_zero_iff.mp h0))
    (1 * (z.length + 1) ^ 1) (divInit z) (divInv_init z)
    (by simp [divInit]; have := length_pairFstD_le z; omega)
  obtain ⟨R, r, q, he, -, -, hv⟩ :=
    iterate_invariant (DivInv z) (fun _ h => (divInv_step h).1) (1 * (z.length + 1) ^ 1)
      (divInv_init z)
  rw [he] at hμ
  simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, List.length_eq_zero_iff] at hμ
  subst hμ
  obtain ⟨hv1, hv2⟩ := hv hb
  simp only [List.length_nil, pow_zero, mul_one, List.reverse_nil, bitsVal, add_zero] at hv1
  rw [divLoop, he]
  simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode]
  exact ((Nat.div_mod_unique hb).mpr ⟨by rw [← hv1]; ring, hv2⟩).imp Eq.symm Eq.symm

/-- **Binary division is polynomial-time** (infrastructure for [AB09 §7.2]; not itself a
result of the book): `0` for a zero divisor, else the normalized quotient slot of the
division loop. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_div : PolyTimeComputable div := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_ite (polyTimeComputable_isZero.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
    (polyTimeComputable_const [])
    (polyTimeComputable_normBits.comp (polyTimeComputable_slot4.comp polyTimeComputable_divLoop))
    using 1
  funext z
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, div]
  by_cases hb : bitsVal (pairSndD z) = 0
  · simp [hb, Nat.zero_bits]
  · simp only [hb, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false]
    rw [(divLoop_spec z (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hb)).1]

/-- **Binary remainder is polynomial-time** (infrastructure for [AB09 §7.2]; not itself a
result of the book): `a` for a zero divisor, else the normalized remainder slot of the
division loop. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_mod : PolyTimeComputable mod := by
  have hs3 : PolyTimeComputable (fun S => pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD S))) :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp polyTimeComputable_slot3
  convert polyTimeComputable_ite (polyTimeComputable_isZero.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
    (polyTimeComputable_normBits.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD)
    (polyTimeComputable_normBits.comp (hs3.comp polyTimeComputable_divLoop))
    using 1
  funext z
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, mod]
  by_cases hb : bitsVal (pairSndD z) = 0
  · simp [hb]
  · simp only [hb, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false]
    rw [(divLoop_spec z (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hb)).2]

end BinArith

end Complexity
```

```text
/-

Authors: TCSlib Contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.Basic

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Lists of words in polynomial time

Infrastructure for [AB09 §7.2]; not itself a result of the book. A list of words
`[w₁, …, wₖ]` is the word `⟨w₁, ⟨w₂, … ⟨wₖ, []⟩ …⟩⟩` (`Complexity.BinArith.encWords`). Every word
is read as a list by `Complexity.BinArith.decWords`, which peels first components until the
empty word, so the loops below are specified on all words. Vectors and matrices of numbers
(the determinant of `TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.DetMod`) are lists of such lists.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.BinArith.encWords`, `Complexity.BinArith.decWords` — encoding and reading.
* `Complexity.BinArith.mapW`, `Complexity.BinArith.zipWithW` — map (with a shared parameter)
  and zip of word-level functions over encoded lists.
* `Complexity.BinArith.countW` — the number of entries, in unary.

## Main results

* `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_mapW`, `Complexity.BinArith.mapW_pairEncode`.
* `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_zipWithW`, `Complexity.BinArith.zipWithW_pairEncode`.
* `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_countW`, `Complexity.BinArith.countW_eq`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§7.2.)
-/

namespace Complexity

namespace BinArith

open Turing LogProg

/-! ### Encoding and reading -/

/-- A list of words, as the concatenation of the pairs `⟨w, []⟩`. -/
def encWords (L : List (List Bool)) : List Bool := L.flatMap (fun w => pairEncode w [])

/-- A pair with empty second component, followed by `b`, is the pair `⟨a, b⟩`. -/
theorem pairEncode_nil_append (a b : List Bool) : pairEncode a [] ++ b = pairEncode a b := by
  simp [pairEncode]

/-- The empty list is the empty word. -/
@[simp] theorem encWords_nil : encWords [] = [] := rfl

/-- `encWords (w :: L) = ⟨w, encWords L⟩`. -/
@[simp] theorem encWords_cons (w : List Bool) (L : List (List Bool)) :
    encWords (w :: L) = pairEncode w (encWords L) := by
  simp [encWords, pairEncode_nil_append]

/-- Appending one word at the end of an encoded list. -/
theorem encWords_append_singleton (L : List (List Bool)) (w : List Bool) :
    encWords (L ++ [w]) = encWords L ++ pairEncode w [] := by
  simp [encWords]

/-- The length of an encoded list. -/
theorem length_encWords (L : List (List Bool)) :
    (encWords L).length = (L.map (fun w => 2 * w.length + 2)).sum := by
  induction L with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons w L ih => simp [length_pairEncode, ih]

/-- An encoded list of `k` words of length at most `c` has length at most `k(2c + 2)`. -/
theorem length_encWords_le (L : List (List Bool)) (c : ℕ) (h : ∀ w ∈ L, w.length ≤ c) :
    (encWords L).length ≤ L.length * (2 * c + 2) := by
  induction L with
  | nil => simp
  | cons w L ih =>
    simp only [encWords_cons, length_pairEncode, List.length_cons]
    have h1 := h w (by simp)
    have h2 := ih (fun v hv => h v (by simp [hv]))
    nlinarith

/-- The second projection of a nonempty word is strictly shorter. -/
theorem length_pairSndD_lt {w : List Bool} (h : w ≠ []) : (pairSndD w).length < w.length := by
  cases hd : pairDecode w with
  | none => simp [pairSndD, hd]; exact List.length_pos_iff.mpr h
  | some ab =>
    obtain ⟨a, b⟩ := ab
    have hz := eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode w a b hd
    rw [hz, pairSndD_pairEncode, length_pairEncode]
    omega

/-- Read a word as a list of words: peel first components until the empty word. -/
def decWords (w : List Bool) : List (List Bool) :=
  if _h : w = [] then [] else pairFstD w :: decWords (pairSndD w)
termination_by w.length
decreasing_by exact length_pairSndD_lt ‹_›

/-- The reading of the empty word. -/
@[simp] theorem decWords_nil : decWords [] = [] := by rw [decWords]; simp

/-- The reading of a nonempty word. -/
theorem decWords_of_ne {w : List Bool} (h : w ≠ []) :
    decWords w = pairFstD w :: decWords (pairSndD w) := by
  rw [decWords]; simp [h]

/-- Reading an encoded list gives the list back. -/
@[simp] theorem decWords_encWords (L : List (List Bool)) : decWords (encWords L) = L := by
  induction L with
  | nil => simp
  | cons w L ih =>
    rw [encWords_cons, decWords_of_ne (by simp [pairEncode]), pairFstD_pairEncode,
      pairSndD_pairEncode, ih]

/-- A word holds at most as many list entries as it has letters. -/
theorem length_decWords_le (w : List Bool) : (decWords w).length ≤ w.length := by
  by_cases hw : w = []
  · simp [hw]
  · rw [decWords_of_ne hw, List.length_cons]
    have := length_pairSndD_lt hw
    have := length_decWords_le (pairSndD w)
    omega
termination_by w.length
decreasing_by exact length_pairSndD_lt hw

/-- Every entry of a word's list is no longer than the word. -/
theorem length_le_of_mem_decWords {w x : List Bool} (hx : x ∈ decWords w) :
    x.length ≤ w.length := by
  by_cases hw : w = []
  · simp [hw] at hx
  · rw [decWords_of_ne hw, List.mem_cons] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | hx
    · exact length_pairFstD_le w
    · have := length_pairSndD_lt hw
      have := length_le_of_mem_decWords hx
      omega
termination_by w.length
decreasing_by exact length_pairSndD_lt hw

/-! ### The list loop -/

/-- Iterated second projections stay inside the word. -/
theorem length_iterate_pairSndD_le (w : List Bool) (i : ℕ) :
    (pairSndD^[i] w).length ≤ w.length := by
  induction i with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ i ih => rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']; exact (length_pairSndD_le _).trans ih

/-- The emptiness of iterated second projections of the empty word. -/
theorem iterate_pairSndD_nil (i : ℕ) : pairSndD^[i] ([] : List Bool) = [] :=
  Function.iterate_fixed rfl i

/-- **The list loop**: over `N ≥ |w|` rounds, emitting `c x` for the head `x` of each nonempty
suffix `pairSndD^[i] w` outputs the concatenation of `c` over the list read from `w`. -/
theorem flatMap_listLoop (c : List Bool → List Bool) :
    ∀ (N : ℕ) (w : List Bool), w.length ≤ N →
      (List.range N).flatMap (fun i => if pairSndD^[i] w = [] then []
        else c (pairFstD (pairSndD^[i] w))) = (decWords w).flatMap c := by
  intro N
  induction N with
  | zero => intro w hw; simp [List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by omega : w.length = 0)]
  | succ N ih =>
    intro w hw
    rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_map]
    simp only [Function.iterate_zero_apply, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Function.iterate_succ_apply]
    by_cases h : w = []
    · subst h
      have := ih [] (by simp)
      simp only [pairSndD, pairDecode, Option.map_none, Option.getD_none, if_true,
        List.nil_append] at this ⊢
      simpa using this
    · rw [if_neg h, ih (pairSndD w) (by have := length_pairSndD_lt h; omega),
        decWords_of_ne h, List.flatMap_cons]

/-! ### Map -/

/-- One round of the map loop on `⟨q, list⟩`: drop the head entry. -/
private def listStep (S : List Bool) : List Bool := pairEncode (pairFstD S) (pairSndD (pairSndD S))

/-- The chunk of the map loop on `⟨q, list⟩`: `⟨g ⟨q, head⟩, []⟩` for a nonempty list. -/
private def mapChunk (g : List Bool → List Bool) (S : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if pairSndD S = [] then []
  else pairEncode (g (pairEncode (pairFstD S) (pairFstD (pairSndD S)))) []

/-- The map loop on `⟨q, list⟩` applying `g ⟨q, ·⟩` to every entry. -/
def mapW (g : List Bool → List Bool) (S : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (List.range (1 * (S.length + 1) ^ 1 + 1)).flatMap (fun i => mapChunk g (listStep^[i] S))

/-- The iterates of the map loop from `⟨q, w⟩`. -/
private theorem iterate_listStep (q w : List Bool) (i : ℕ) :
    listStep^[i] (pairEncode q w) = pairEncode q (pairSndD^[i] w) := by
  induction i with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ i ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih, Function.iterate_succ_apply']
    simp [listStep]

/-- **The map loop maps**: on `⟨q, w⟩` it outputs the encoded list `g ⟨q, x⟩` over the entries
`x` read from `w`. -/
theorem mapW_pairEncode (g : List Bool → List Bool) (q w : List Bool) :
    mapW g (pairEncode q w) = encWords ((decWords w).map (fun x => g (pairEncode q x))) := by
  unfold mapW
  simp only [iterate_listStep, mapChunk, pairSndD_pairEncode, pairFstD_pairEncode]
  rw [flatMap_listLoop (fun x => pairEncode (g (pairEncode q x)) []) _ w
    (by simp [length_pairEncode]; omega)]
  simp [encWords, List.flatMap_map]

/-- **The map loop is polynomial-time** for a polynomial-time `g`.

**Proof sketch.** The round drops the head entry and the emitted chunk is `g` of it; after
`i` rounds the state is `⟨q, l⟩` with `l` a suffix of the input list (`iterate_listStep`), so
the emit loop `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_emitIter` applies with a linear bound. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_mapW {g : List Bool → List Bool} (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) :
    PolyTimeComputable (mapW g) := by
  have hs : PolyTimeComputable listStep :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode polyTimeComputable_slot3
  have he : PolyTimeComputable (mapChunk g) := by
    unfold mapChunk
    convert polyTimeComputable_ite (polyTimeComputable_isNil.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
      (polyTimeComputable_const [])
      ((hg.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode polyTimeComputable_slot2)).pairEncode
        (polyTimeComputable_const [])) using 1
    funext S; simp
  refine polyTimeComputable_emitIter hs he 1 1 2 1 (fun w i => ?_)
  cases i with
  | zero => simp; omega
  | succ i =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply, show listStep w = pairEncode (pairFstD w) (pairSndD
      (pairSndD w)) from rfl, iterate_listStep, length_pairEncode]
    have h1 := length_iterate_pairSndD_le (pairSndD (pairSndD w)) i
    have h2 := length_pair_components_le w
    have h3 := length_pairSndD_le (pairSndD w)
    simp; omega

/-! ### Zip -/

/-- One round of the zip loop on `⟨q, ⟨l₁, l₂⟩⟩`: drop the head entries of both lists. -/
private def zipStep (S : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (pairFstD S)
    (pairEncode (pairSndD (pairFstD (pairSndD S))) (pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD S))))

/-- The chunk of the zip loop: `⟨g ⟨q, ⟨x, y⟩⟩, []⟩` for the heads `x`, `y` of two nonempty
lists. -/
private def zipChunk (g : List Bool → List Bool) (S : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if pairFstD (pairSndD S) = [] ∨ pairSndD (pairSndD S) = [] then []
  else pairEncode (g (pairEncode (pairFstD S) (pairEncode (pairFstD (pairFstD (pairSndD S)))
    (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD S)))))) []

/-- The zip loop on `⟨q, ⟨l₁, l₂⟩⟩` applying `g ⟨q, ⟨x, y⟩⟩` to paired entries. -/
def zipWithW (g : List Bool → List Bool) (S : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (List.range (1 * (S.length + 1) ^ 1 + 1)).flatMap (fun i => zipChunk g (zipStep^[i] S))

/-- The iterates of the zip loop from `⟨q, ⟨l₁, l₂⟩⟩`. -/
private theorem iterate_zipStep (q l₁ l₂ : List Bool) (i : ℕ) :
    zipStep^[i] (pairEncode q (pairEncode l₁ l₂)) =
      pairEncode q (pairEncode (pairSndD^[i] l₁) (pairSndD^[i] l₂)) := by
  induction i with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ i ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih, Function.iterate_succ_apply',
      Function.iterate_succ_apply']
    simp [zipStep]

/-- The zip loop body over `N ≥ |l₁|` rounds zips the two lists read from `l₁`, `l₂`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `N`: round `0` emits `c` of the two head entries, or nothing
when a list is empty, and the remaining rounds are the statement for the tails
(`decWords_of_ne`). -/
private theorem flatMap_zipLoop (c : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool) :
    ∀ (N : ℕ) (l₁ l₂ : List Bool), l₁.length ≤ N →
      (List.range N).flatMap (fun i =>
        if pairSndD^[i] l₁ = [] ∨ pairSndD^[i] l₂ = [] then []
        else c (pairFstD (pairSndD^[i] l₁)) (pairFstD (pairSndD^[i] l₂))) =
        (List.zipWith c (decWords l₁) (decWords l₂)).flatMap id := by
  intro N
  induction N with
  | zero =>
    intro l₁ l₂ h
    simp [List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by omega : l₁.length = 0)]
  | succ N ih =>
    intro l₁ l₂ h
    rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_map]
    simp only [Function.iterate_zero_apply, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Function.iterate_succ_apply]
    have hlen : (pairSndD l₁).length ≤ N := by
      by_cases h1 : l₁ = []
      · subst h1; simp [pairSndD, pairDecode]
      · have := length_pairSndD_lt h1; omega
    rw [ih (pairSndD l₁) (pairSndD l₂) hlen]
    by_cases h1 : l₁ = []
    · subst h1; simp [show pairSndD ([] : List Bool) = [] from rfl]
    by_cases h2 : l₂ = []
    · subst h2; simp [show pairSndD ([] : List Bool) = [] from rfl]
    rw [if_neg (by tauto), decWords_of_ne h1, decWords_of_ne h2]
    simp

/-- **The zip loop zips**: on `⟨q, ⟨l₁, l₂⟩⟩` it outputs the encoded list of `g ⟨q, ⟨x, y⟩⟩`
over the paired entries read from `l₁` and `l₂` (truncated to the shorter list). -/
theorem zipWithW_pairEncode (g : List Bool → List Bool) (q l₁ l₂ : List Bool) :
    zipWithW g (pairEncode q (pairEncode l₁ l₂)) =
      encWords (List.zipWith (fun x y => g (pairEncode q (pairEncode x y)))
        (decWords l₁) (decWords l₂)) := by
  unfold zipWithW
  simp only [iterate_zipStep, zipChunk, pairSndD_pairEncode, pairFstD_pairEncode]
  rw [flatMap_zipLoop (fun x y => pairEncode (g (pairEncode q (pairEncode x y))) []) _ l₁ l₂
    (by simp [length_pairEncode]; omega)]
  simp [encWords, List.flatMap_def, List.map_zipWith]

/-- **The zip loop is polynomial-time** for a polynomial-time `g`.

**Proof sketch.** As for `polyTimeComputable_mapW`: the round drops the head entries of both
lists, the chunk is `g` of them, and the iterates keep suffixes of the input
(`iterate_zipStep`), so `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_emitIter` applies. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_zipWithW {g : List Bool → List Bool} (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) :
    PolyTimeComputable (zipWithW g) := by
  have hl1 : PolyTimeComputable (fun S => pairFstD (pairSndD S)) := polyTimeComputable_slot2
  have hl2 : PolyTimeComputable (fun S => pairSndD (pairSndD S)) := polyTimeComputable_slot3
  have hs : PolyTimeComputable zipStep :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode ((polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp hl1).pairEncode
      (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp hl2))
  have he : PolyTimeComputable (zipChunk g) := by
    unfold zipChunk
    convert polyTimeComputable_ite
      (polyTimeComputable_or (polyTimeComputable_isNil.comp hl1)
        (polyTimeComputable_isNil.comp hl2)) (polyTimeComputable_const [])
      ((hg.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode
        ((polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp hl1).pairEncode
          (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp hl2)))).pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_const []))
      using 1
    funext S; simp
  refine polyTimeComputable_emitIter hs he 1 1 5 1 (fun w i => ?_)
  cases i with
  | zero => simp; omega
  | succ i =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply, show zipStep w = pairEncode (pairFstD w)
      (pairEncode (pairSndD (pairFstD (pairSndD w))) (pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD w))))
      from rfl, iterate_zipStep, length_pairEncode, length_pairEncode]
    have h1 := length_iterate_pairSndD_le (pairSndD (pairFstD (pairSndD w))) i
    have h2 := length_iterate_pairSndD_le (pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD w))) i
    have h3 := length_pair_components_le w
    have h4 := length_pair_components_le (pairSndD w)
    have h5 := length_pairSndD_le (pairFstD (pairSndD w))
    have h6 := length_pairSndD_le (pairSndD (pairSndD w))
    simp; omega

/-! ### Counting -/

/-- The number of entries of the list read from `w`, in unary. -/
def countW (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (List.range (1 * (w.length + 1) ^ 1 + 1)).flatMap
    (fun i => if pairSndD^[i] w = [] then [] else [true])

/-- `countW w` is `1^k` for the number `k` of entries read from `w`. -/
theorem countW_eq (w : List Bool) : countW w = List.replicate (decWords w).length true := by
  unfold countW
  rw [flatMap_listLoop (fun _ => [true]) _ w (by simp; omega)]
  induction decWords w with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons x L ih => simp [ih, List.replicate_succ]

/-- **Counting the entries is polynomial-time.** -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_countW : PolyTimeComputable countW := by
  have he : PolyTimeComputable (fun w : List Bool => if w = [] then [] else [true]) := by
    convert polyTimeComputable_ite polyTimeComputable_isNil (polyTimeComputable_const [])
      (polyTimeComputable_const [true]) using 1
    funext w; simp
  exact polyTimeComputable_emitIter polyTimeComputable_pairSndD he 1 1 1 1 (fun w i => by
    have := length_iterate_pairSndD_le w i; simp; omega)

end BinArith

end Complexity
```


## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/CircuitComplexity/UnaryCode.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import Mathlib.Data.List.Basic

/-!
# The unary code of a natural number

The self-delimiting code `1ᵏ0` of a natural number `k`, and its parser.  Every circuit
description of the library writes its numbers this way: the formula encoding of
`Encoding.lean` (for `CKT-SAT`, [AB09, Def 6.9]), the book-model description
`BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode` of `Uniform.lean` ([AB09, Def 6.12]), and its parser
`BoolCircuit.decodeDAG` in `DAGCircuitSatLang.lean`.

## Main definitions

* `BoolCircuit.encodeNat` — `k ↦ 1ᵏ0`.
* `BoolCircuit.decodeNat` — read one unary number off the front of a bit string.

## Main results

* `BoolCircuit.decodeNat_encodeNat` — reading back a code returns its number and the
  untouched rest.

## Divergences from [AB09]

* [AB09] fixes no representation of numbers inside circuit descriptions.  Unary costs a
  polynomial factor over binary (`O(n)` rather than `O(log n)` bits for an index below
  `n`), which every polynomial bound downstream absorbs.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.  (§6.1.2 and §6.2: string descriptions of circuits.)
-/

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

namespace BoolCircuit

/-- The unary code `1ᵏ0` of a natural number: `k` `true`s terminated by a `false`. -/
def encodeNat (k : ℕ) : List Bool := List.replicate k true ++ [false]

/-- Read a unary number `1ᵏ0` (`BoolCircuit.encodeNat`) off the front of a string,
returning it and the rest; `none` if the string ends before the terminating `0`. -/
def decodeNat : List Bool → Option (ℕ × List Bool)
  | [] => none
  | false :: r => some (0, r)
  | true :: r => (decodeNat r).map fun p => (p.1 + 1, p.2)

/-- Reading back a unary code returns its number and the untouched rest. -/
theorem decodeNat_encodeNat (k : ℕ) (r : List Bool) :
    decodeNat (encodeNat k ++ r) = some (k, r) := by
  induction k with
  | zero => simp [encodeNat, decodeNat]
  | succ k ih =>
    have h : encodeNat (k + 1) ++ r = true :: (encodeNat k ++ r) := by
      simp [encodeNat, List.replicate_succ]
    rw [h, decodeNat, ih]
    rfl

end BoolCircuit
```


## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/ClassP/BinaryArith/Loops.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 The TCSlib Authors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib Contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.Iterate
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.AddSub
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.Mul
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.Div
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.Words
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.Transducer
import TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.UnaryCode
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimePrefix

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Counted loops, unary numbers and word tools in polynomial time

Generic polynomial-time word functions on `Turing.pairEncode`-structured inputs, shared by
the randomized algorithms of [AB09, §7.2.3–7.2.4]: a counted loop (a host: run a step once
per letter of a unary counter), the reading of unary numbers, the lookup of an entry in an
encoded list of words (`Complexity.BinArith.encWords`), word equality, unary multiplication,
and the cutting of a word into blocks. Not themselves results of the book.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.BinArith.forLoop` — run a step once per letter of a unary counter.
* `Complexity.BinArith.uHead`, `Complexity.BinArith.uRest`, `Complexity.BinArith.hasFalse` —
  the leading `1`s of a word, the rest after the first `0`, and whether there is a `0`.
* `Complexity.BinArith.getW` — the `j`-th entry of an encoded list of words.
* `Complexity.BinArith.eqW` — equality of the two components of a pair.
* `Complexity.BinArith.mulU` — unary multiplication (`|a|` copies of `b` on `⟨a, b⟩`).
* `Complexity.BinArith.chunkW`, `Complexity.BinArith.chunkList` — cutting a word into blocks
  of `|c|` bits, as a list of words.

## Main results

* `Complexity.BinArith.forLoop_pairEncode`, `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_forLoop`,
  `Complexity.BinArith.forLoop_bound_of_ctx` — the counted loop and its time bound.
* `Complexity.BinArith.decodeNat_eq` — `BoolCircuit.decodeNat` through `uHead` and `uRest`.
* `Complexity.BinArith.getW_pairEncode`, `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_getW`.
* `Complexity.BinArith.eqW_pairEncode`, `Complexity.BinArith.length_mulU`,
  `Complexity.BinArith.chunkW_pairEncode` — what they compute, and their
  `polyTimeComputable_*` lemmas.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.
-/

namespace Complexity

namespace BinArith

open Turing
open Complexity.LogProg (bitsVal eq_of_bitsVal_eq)

/-- Composition in applied form: `x ↦ f (g x)` is polynomial-time when `f` and `g` are.  (Stated
with an applied body so that unification never unfolds `f`.) -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_app {f g : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) : PolyTimeComputable (fun x => f (g x)) :=
  hf.comp hg

/-- A one-bit test of a polynomial-time function, in applied form. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_test_app {p : List Bool → Bool} {g : List Bool → List Bool}
    (hp : PolyTimeComputable (fun x => [p x])) (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun x => [p (g x)]) :=
  hp.comp hg

/-! ### The counted loop -/

/-- One round of the counted loop on `⟨c, d⟩`: if `c ≠ []`, drop a letter of `c` and apply
`f` to `d`; a state with empty (or malformed) counter is fixed. -/
def forStep (f : List Bool → List Bool) (S : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if isNilB (pairFstD S) then S else pairEncode ((pairFstD S).drop 1) (f (pairSndD S))

/-- The counted loop: `|S| + 1` rounds of `forStep f` from `S`. -/
def forLoop (f : List Bool → List Bool) (S : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (forStep f)^[1 * (S.length + 1) ^ 1] S

/-- The rounds of the counted loop from `⟨c, d⟩`. -/
theorem iterate_forStep (f : List Bool → List Bool) (c d : List Bool) (i : ℕ) :
    (forStep f)^[i] (pairEncode c d) = pairEncode (c.drop i) (f^[min i c.length] d) := by
  induction i with
  | zero => simp
  | succ i ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih]
    by_cases hi : c.length ≤ i
    · have h1 : min i c.length = c.length := by omega
      have h2 : min (i + 1) c.length = c.length := by omega
      simp [forStep, isNilB, List.drop_eq_nil_of_le hi, List.drop_eq_nil_of_le (by omega :
        c.length ≤ i + 1), h1, h2]
    · have hne : c.drop i ≠ [] := by simp; omega
      have h1 : min i c.length = i := by omega
      have h2 : min (i + 1) c.length = i + 1 := by omega
      simp only [forStep, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, isNilB, hne,
        decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, List.drop_drop, h1, h2,
        Function.iterate_succ_apply']

/-- **The counted loop runs `f` once per letter of the counter**:
`forLoop f ⟨c, d⟩ = ⟨[], f^[|c|] d⟩`. -/
theorem forLoop_pairEncode (f : List Bool → List Bool) (c d : List Bool) :
    forLoop f (pairEncode c d) = pairEncode [] (f^[c.length] d) := by
  unfold forLoop
  rw [iterate_forStep, List.drop_eq_nil_of_le (by simp [length_pairEncode]; omega)]
  congr 2
  simp [length_pairEncode]
  omega

/-- A state whose counter is empty is fixed by the round. -/
theorem forStep_of_fst_nil (f : List Bool → List Bool) {S : List Bool} (h : pairFstD S = []) :
    forStep f S = S := by
  simp [forStep, isNilB, h]

/-- **The counted loop is polynomial-time** when its body is and the iterates `f^[j] d`,
`j ≤ |c|`, stay inside a polynomial envelope of `|⟨c, d⟩|`.

**Proof sketch.** `forLoop f` is `polyTimeComputable_iterate` of the round `forStep f` (an
`ite` of polynomial-time pieces) from the input. A word that is not a pair has empty counter
and is fixed; on `⟨c, d⟩` the `i`-th iterate is `⟨c.drop i, f^[min i |c|] d⟩`
(`iterate_forStep`), whose length the envelope bounds. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_forLoop {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (B b : ℕ) (hbound : ∀ c d j, j ≤ c.length →
      (f^[j] d).length ≤ B * ((pairEncode c d).length + 1) ^ b) :
    PolyTimeComputable (forLoop f) := by
  have hstep : PolyTimeComputable (forStep f) := by
    unfold forStep
    exact polyTimeComputable_ite (polyTimeComputable_isNil.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD)
      polyTimeComputable_id
      ((polyTimeComputable_tail.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD).pairEncode
        (hf.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD))
  refine polyTimeComputable_iterate hstep polyTimeComputable_id 1 1 (B + 2) (b + 1)
    (fun S i _ => ?_)
  simp only [id]
  have hP : 1 ≤ (S.length + 1) ^ b := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by omega)
  have hpow : (S.length + 1) ^ (b + 1) = (S.length + 1) ^ b * (S.length + 1) := pow_succ _ _
  have h5 : S.length + 1 ≤ (S.length + 1) ^ b * (S.length + 1) := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left _ hP
  rw [hpow]
  cases hd : pairDecode S with
  | none =>
    have h0 : pairFstD S = [] := by simp [pairFstD, hd]
    rw [Function.iterate_fixed (forStep_of_fst_nil f h0)]
    nlinarith
  | some cd =>
    obtain ⟨c, d⟩ := cd
    have hS := eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode S c d hd
    have h1 := hbound c d (min i c.length) (by omega)
    rw [← hS] at h1
    rw [hS, iterate_forStep, length_pairEncode]
    rw [← hS]
    have h2 : (c.drop i).length ≤ c.length := by simp
    have h3 : 2 * c.length + 2 ≤ S.length := by rw [hS]; simp [length_pairEncode]
    have h6 : B * (S.length + 1) ^ b ≤ B * ((S.length + 1) ^ b * (S.length + 1)) :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega))
    nlinarith

/-- An iterate bound for context-preserving bodies: if `f ⟨q, ·⟩` keeps `q` and grows the
word by at most `A(|q| + 1)`, then `|f^[j] d| ≤ |d| + jA(|q| + 1)`. -/
theorem length_iterate_le_of_ctx {f : List Bool → List Bool} (A : ℕ)
    (hctx : ∀ d, pairFstD (f d) = pairFstD d)
    (hlen : ∀ d, (f d).length ≤ d.length + A * ((pairFstD d).length + 1)) (d : List Bool) (j : ℕ) :
    (f^[j] d).length ≤ d.length + j * (A * ((pairFstD d).length + 1)) := by
  have hq : ∀ j, pairFstD (f^[j] d) = pairFstD d := by
    intro j
    induction j with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ j ih => rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', hctx, ih]
  induction j with
  | zero => simp
  | succ j ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
    have := hlen (f^[j] d)
    rw [hq j] at this
    rw [Nat.succ_mul]
    omega

/-- The envelope required by `polyTimeComputable_forLoop`, for context-preserving bodies of
bounded growth. -/
theorem forLoop_bound_of_ctx {f : List Bool → List Bool} (A : ℕ)
    (hctx : ∀ d, pairFstD (f d) = pairFstD d)
    (hlen : ∀ d, (f d).length ≤ d.length + A * ((pairFstD d).length + 1)) :
    ∀ c d j, j ≤ c.length → (f^[j] d).length ≤ (A + 1) * ((pairEncode c d).length + 1) ^ 2 := by
  intro c d j hj
  have h := length_iterate_le_of_ctx A hctx hlen d j
  have hq := length_pairFstD_le d
  have hN : c.length + d.length ≤ (pairEncode c d).length := by simp [length_pairEncode]; omega
  set N := (pairEncode c d).length
  have h1 : j * (A * ((pairFstD d).length + 1)) ≤ N * (A * (N + 1)) :=
    Nat.mul_le_mul (by omega) (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega))
  nlinarith

/-! ### Unary numbers -/

/-- The transition of `uHead`: stay live while reading `1`s. -/
private def headδ (q b : Bool) : Bool := q && b

/-- The emission of `uHead`: copy the `1`s of the live phase. -/
private def headO (q b : Bool) : Option Bool := if q && b then some true else none

/-- The leading `1`s of a word (`1ʲ` on `1ʲ0w`). -/
def uHead (w : List Bool) : List Bool := transduce headδ headO true w

/-- The transition of `uRest`: switch on at the first `0`. -/
private def restδ (q b : Bool) : Bool := q || !b

/-- The emission of `uRest`: copy everything after the first `0`. -/
private def restO (q b : Bool) : Option Bool := if q then some b else none

/-- The word after the first `0` (`w` on `1ʲ0w`; `[]` if there is no `0`). -/
def uRest (w : List Bool) : List Bool := transduce restδ restO false w

/-- Whether a word contains a `0`. -/
def hasFalse (w : List Bool) : Bool := (w.map not).any id

/-- The `uHead` transducer emits nothing once off. -/
private theorem transduce_head_false (w : List Bool) : transduce headδ headO false w = [] := by
  induction w with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b w ih => simp [transduce, headδ, headO, ih]

/-- The `uRest` transducer copies everything once on. -/
private theorem transduce_rest_true (w : List Bool) : transduce restδ restO true w = w := by
  induction w with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b w ih => simp [transduce, restδ, restO, ih]

/-- `uHead` on `0w` is empty. -/
@[simp] theorem uHead_false_cons (w : List Bool) : uHead (false :: w) = [] := by
  simp [uHead, transduce, headδ, headO, transduce_head_false]

/-- `uHead` on `1w`. -/
@[simp] theorem uHead_true_cons (w : List Bool) : uHead (true :: w) = true :: uHead w := by
  simp [uHead, transduce, headδ, headO]

/-- `uRest` on `0w` is `w`. -/
@[simp] theorem uRest_false_cons (w : List Bool) : uRest (false :: w) = w := by
  simp [uRest, transduce, restδ, restO, transduce_rest_true]

/-- `uRest` on `1w`. -/
@[simp] theorem uRest_true_cons (w : List Bool) : uRest (true :: w) = uRest w := by
  simp [uRest, transduce, restδ, restO]

/-- `uHead []` is empty. -/
@[simp] theorem uHead_nil : uHead [] = [] := rfl

/-- `uRest []` is empty. -/
@[simp] theorem uRest_nil : uRest [] = [] := rfl

/-- `hasFalse` on a cons. -/
@[simp] theorem hasFalse_cons (b : Bool) (w : List Bool) :
    hasFalse (b :: w) = (!b || hasFalse w) := by
  simp [hasFalse]

/-- `[]` has no `0`. -/
@[simp] theorem hasFalse_nil : hasFalse [] = false := rfl

/-- **Reading a unary number**: `decodeNat w` is `(|uHead w|, uRest w)` if `w` has a `0`. -/
theorem decodeNat_eq (w : List Bool) :
    BoolCircuit.decodeNat w =
      if hasFalse w then some ((uHead w).length, uRest w) else none := by
  induction w with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b w ih =>
    cases b
    · simp [BoolCircuit.decodeNat]
    · simp only [BoolCircuit.decodeNat, ih, uHead_true_cons, uRest_true_cons, hasFalse_cons,
        Bool.not_true, Bool.false_or, List.length_cons]
      split <;> simp

/-- Reading `1ʲ0w`. -/
theorem uHead_encodeNat (j : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
    uHead (BoolCircuit.encodeNat j ++ w) = List.replicate j true := by
  induction j with
  | zero => simp [BoolCircuit.encodeNat]
  | succ j ih => simpa [BoolCircuit.encodeNat, List.replicate_succ] using ih

/-- The rest of `1ʲ0w` is `w`. -/
theorem uRest_encodeNat (j : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
    uRest (BoolCircuit.encodeNat j ++ w) = w := by
  induction j with
  | zero => simp [BoolCircuit.encodeNat]
  | succ j ih => simpa [BoolCircuit.encodeNat, List.replicate_succ] using ih

/-- `1ʲ0w` has a `0`. -/
theorem hasFalse_encodeNat (j : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
    hasFalse (BoolCircuit.encodeNat j ++ w) = true := by
  induction j with
  | zero => simp [BoolCircuit.encodeNat]
  | succ j ih => simpa [BoolCircuit.encodeNat, List.replicate_succ] using ih

/-- A word with a `0` is `1ʲ0w` for `1ʲ = uHead`, `w = uRest`. -/
theorem eq_encodeNat_of_hasFalse {w : List Bool} (h : hasFalse w = true) :
    w = BoolCircuit.encodeNat (uHead w).length ++ uRest w := by
  induction w with
  | nil => simp at h
  | cons b w ih =>
    cases b
    · simp [BoolCircuit.encodeNat]
    · simp only [hasFalse_cons, Bool.not_true, Bool.false_or] at h
      have := ih h
      simp only [uHead_true_cons, uRest_true_cons, List.length_cons, BoolCircuit.encodeNat,
        List.replicate_succ, List.cons_append] at this ⊢
      exact congrArg _ this

/-- `uRest w` is no longer than `w`. -/
theorem length_uRest_le (w : List Bool) : (uRest w).length ≤ w.length := by
  induction w with
  | nil => simp
  | cons b w ih =>
    cases b
    · simp
    · simp only [uRest_true_cons, List.length_cons]; omega

/-- `uHead w` is no longer than `w`. -/
theorem length_uHead_le (w : List Bool) : (uHead w).length ≤ w.length := by
  induction w with
  | nil => simp
  | cons b w ih =>
    cases b
    · simp
    · simp only [uHead_true_cons, List.length_cons]; omega

/-- `uHead` is polynomial-time (a one-pass transducer). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_uHead : PolyTimeComputable uHead :=
  polyTimeComputable_transduce headδ headO true

/-- `uRest` is polynomial-time (a one-pass transducer). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_uRest : PolyTimeComputable uRest :=
  polyTimeComputable_transduce restδ restO false

/-- `hasFalse` is polynomial-time (negate, then test for a `1`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_hasFalse : PolyTimeComputable (fun w => [hasFalse w]) := by
  have hneg : PolyTimeComputable (transduce (σ := Unit) (fun _ _ => ()) (fun _ b => some !b) ()) :=
    polyTimeComputable_transduce _ _ ()
  have heq : ∀ w : List Bool,
      transduce (σ := Unit) (fun _ _ => ()) (fun _ b => some !b) () w = w.map not := by
    intro w
    induction w with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons b w ih => simp [transduce, ih]
  convert polyTimeComputable_any.comp hneg using 1
  funext w
  simp [hasFalse, heq]

/-! ### Lookup in a list of words -/

/-- The entry of index `|J|` of the list encoded in `L`, on `⟨J, L⟩` (`[]` past the end). -/
def getW (z : List Bool) : List Bool := pairFstD (pairSndD (forLoop pairSndD z))

/-- Peeling `j` entries of an encoded list. -/
theorem iterate_pairSndD_encWords (L : List (List Bool)) (j : ℕ) :
    pairSndD^[j] (encWords L) = encWords (L.drop j) := by
  induction j generalizing L with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ j ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply]
    cases L with
    | nil => exact iterate_pairSndD_nil j
    | cons w L => simp [ih]

/-- **Lookup**: `getW ⟨J, [w₀, …]⟩ = w_{|J|}` (`[]` past the end). -/
theorem getW_pairEncode (J : List Bool) (L : List (List Bool)) :
    getW (pairEncode J (encWords L)) = L.getD J.length [] := by
  rw [getW, forLoop_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, iterate_pairSndD_encWords,
    List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, ← List.head?_drop]
  cases L.drop J.length with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons w L' => simp

/-- Lookup in a list of binary numbers: the value of the entry, `0` past the end. -/
theorem getW_pairEncode_bits (J : List Bool) (vs : List ℕ) :
    getW (pairEncode J (encWords (vs.map Nat.bits))) = Nat.bits (vs.getD J.length 0) := by
  rw [getW_pairEncode]
  simp only [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_map]
  cases vs[J.length]? <;> simp [Nat.zero_bits]

/-- Lookup is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_getW : PolyTimeComputable getW := by
  have hl : PolyTimeComputable (forLoop pairSndD) := by
    refine polyTimeComputable_forLoop polyTimeComputable_pairSndD 1 1 (fun c d j _ => ?_)
    have := length_iterate_pairSndD_le d j
    simp [length_pairEncode]
    omega
  exact polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp hl)

/-! ### Equality, unary multiplication and cutting into blocks -/

/-- Either both projections are empty or the word is the pair of its projections. -/
private theorem pair_cases (z : List Bool) :
    (pairFstD z = [] ∧ pairSndD z = []) ∨ z = pairEncode (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) := by
  cases hd : pairDecode z with
  | none => left; simp [pairFstD, pairSndD, hd]
  | some ab =>
    right
    obtain ⟨a, b⟩ := ab
    simpa [pairFstD, pairSndD, hd] using eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode z a b hd

/-- Word equality on `⟨a, b⟩`: equal lengths and equal values. -/
def eqW (z : List Bool) : Bool :=
  decide ((pairFstD z).length = (pairSndD z).length) && beq z

/-- `eqW ⟨a, b⟩` decides `a = b`. -/
theorem eqW_pairEncode (a b : List Bool) : eqW (pairEncode a b) = decide (a = b) := by
  simp only [eqW, beq, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode]
  by_cases h : a = b
  · simp [h]
  · simp only [h, decide_false, Bool.and_eq_false_iff, decide_eq_false_iff_not]
    by_contra hc
    push_neg at hc
    exact h (eq_of_bitsVal_eq hc.1 hc.2)

/-- Word equality is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_eqW : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [eqW z]) :=
  polyTimeComputable_and polyTimeComputable_lenEq polyTimeComputable_beq

/-- One round of unary multiplication on `⟨b, acc⟩`: append `b` to `acc`. -/
private def mulUStep (d : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (pairFstD d) (pairSndD d ++ pairFstD d)

/-- Unary multiplication: on `⟨a, b⟩`, `|a|` copies of `b`. -/
def mulU (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  pairSndD (pairSndD (forLoop mulUStep (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (pairEncode (pairSndD z) []))))

/-- The rounds of unary multiplication. -/
private theorem iterate_mulUStep (b acc : List Bool) (j : ℕ) :
    mulUStep^[j] (pairEncode b acc) = pairEncode b (acc ++ (List.replicate j b).flatten) := by
  induction j with
  | zero => simp
  | succ j ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih]
    simp [mulUStep, List.replicate_succ', List.flatten_append]

/-- `|mulU ⟨a, b⟩| = |a| · |b|`. -/
theorem length_mulU (a b : List Bool) : (mulU (pairEncode a b)).length = a.length * b.length := by
  simp [mulU, forLoop_pairEncode, iterate_mulUStep, List.length_flatten, List.sum_replicate]

/-- Unary multiplication is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_mulU : PolyTimeComputable mulU := by
  have hs : PolyTimeComputable mulUStep :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.append
      polyTimeComputable_pairFstD)
  have hl := polyTimeComputable_forLoop hs 3 2 (forLoop_bound_of_ctx 2
    (fun d => by simp [mulUStep]) (fun d => by
      rcases pair_cases d with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | h
      · simp [mulUStep, h1, h2, length_pairEncode]
      · obtain ⟨a, b, rfl⟩ : ∃ a b, d = pairEncode a b := ⟨_, _, h⟩
        simp [mulUStep, length_pairEncode]; omega))
  exact polyTimeComputable_slot3.comp (hl.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode
    (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_const []))))

/-- One round of cutting on `⟨c, ⟨rest, acc⟩⟩`: move the first `|c|` bits of `rest` to a new
entry of the word list `acc`; fixed once `rest` is empty. -/
private def chunkStep (d : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if isNilB (pairFstD (pairSndD d)) then d
  else pairEncode (pairFstD d)
    (pairEncode (PrefixByLength.drop (pairEncode (pairFstD d) (pairFstD (pairSndD d))))
      (pairSndD (pairSndD d) ++
        pairEncode (PrefixByLength.take (pairEncode (pairFstD d) (pairFstD (pairSndD d)))) []))

/-- Cutting `w` into blocks of `|c|` bits, on `⟨c, w⟩`; the result is a word list. -/
def chunkW (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD (forLoop chunkStep
    (pairEncode (pairSndD z) (pairEncode (pairFstD z) (pairEncode (pairSndD z) []))))))

/-- The first `N` blocks of `c` bits of `w`. -/
def chunkList (c : ℕ) (w : List Bool) (N : ℕ) : List (List Bool) :=
  (List.range N).map fun i => (w.drop (i * c)).take c

/-- A round of cutting on a genuine state. -/
private theorem chunkStep_pairEncode (c rest acc : List Bool) :
    chunkStep (pairEncode c (pairEncode rest acc)) = if rest = [] then
      pairEncode c (pairEncode rest acc) else pairEncode c (pairEncode (rest.drop c.length)
        (acc ++ pairEncode (rest.take c.length) [])) := by
  simp [chunkStep, isNilB, PrefixByLength.take, PrefixByLength.drop]

/-- `N` rounds of cutting a word of `N` blocks. -/
private theorem iterate_chunkStep (c : List Bool) :
    ∀ (N : ℕ) (w : List Bool) (L : List (List Bool)), w.length = N * c.length →
      (0 < c.length ∨ N = 0) → chunkStep^[N] (pairEncode c (pairEncode w (encWords L))) =
        pairEncode c (pairEncode [] (encWords (L ++ chunkList c.length w N)))
  | 0, w, L, h, _ => by simp_all [chunkList]
  | N + 1, w, L, h, hc => by
    have hc' : 0 < c.length := by omega
    have hw : w ≠ [] := by rintro rfl; simp at h; simp [h] at hc'
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply, chunkStep_pairEncode, if_neg hw,
      ← encWords_append_singleton,
      iterate_chunkStep c N _ _ (by simp [h, Nat.succ_mul]) (Or.inl hc')]
    congr 3
    simp only [chunkList, List.range_succ_eq_map, List.map_cons, List.map_map, zero_mul,
      List.drop_zero, List.append_assoc, List.singleton_append]
    congr 2
    refine List.map_congr_left fun i _ => ?_
    simp [List.drop_drop, Nat.succ_mul, Nat.add_comm]

/-- **Cutting into blocks**: if `|w| = N·|c|` then `chunkW ⟨c, w⟩` lists the `N` blocks. -/
theorem chunkW_pairEncode (c w : List Bool) (N : ℕ) (h : w.length = N * c.length)
    (hc : 0 < c.length ∨ N = 0) :
    chunkW (pairEncode c w) = encWords (chunkList c.length w N) := by
  have hN : N ≤ w.length := by
    rcases hc with hc | rfl
    · rw [h]; exact Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ hc
    · exact Nat.zero_le _
  have he := iterate_chunkStep c N w [] h hc
  simp only [encWords, List.flatMap_nil, List.nil_append] at he
  simp only [chunkW, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, forLoop_pairEncode]
  rw [show w.length = (w.length - N) + N by omega, Function.iterate_add_apply, he,
    Function.iterate_fixed (by rw [chunkStep_pairEncode, if_pos rfl])]
  simp [encWords]

/-- Cutting is polynomial-time.

**Proof sketch.** The round is assembled from the projections, the prefix operations and
`polyTimeComputable_ite`; it keeps `c` and grows a genuine state by `2` bits (the moved bits
are re-encoded once), so `forLoop_bound_of_ctx` bounds the counted loop. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_chunkW : PolyTimeComputable chunkW := by
  have hcr := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode polyTimeComputable_slot2
  have hs : PolyTimeComputable chunkStep := by
    unfold chunkStep
    exact polyTimeComputable_ite (polyTimeComputable_isNil.comp polyTimeComputable_slot2)
      polyTimeComputable_id (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode
        ((polyTimeComputable_dropPrefixByLength.comp hcr).pairEncode
          (polyTimeComputable_slot3.append
            ((polyTimeComputable_takePrefixByLength.comp hcr).pairEncode
              (polyTimeComputable_const [])))))
  have hctx : ∀ d, pairFstD (chunkStep d) = pairFstD d := fun d => by
    unfold chunkStep; split_ifs <;> simp
  have hlen : ∀ d, (chunkStep d).length ≤ d.length + 2 * ((pairFstD d).length + 1) := by
    intro d
    by_cases hr : pairFstD (pairSndD d) = []
    · simp [chunkStep, isNilB, hr]
    rcases pair_cases d with ⟨-, h2⟩ | h
    · simp [h2, pairFstD, pairDecode] at hr
    obtain ⟨c, S, rfl⟩ : ∃ c S, d = pairEncode c S := ⟨_, _, h⟩
    simp only [pairSndD_pairEncode] at hr
    rcases pair_cases S with ⟨h1, -⟩ | hS
    · exact absurd h1 hr
    obtain ⟨rest, acc, rfl⟩ : ∃ a b, S = pairEncode a b := ⟨_, _, hS⟩
    simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode] at hr
    rw [chunkStep_pairEncode, if_neg hr]
    simp only [length_pairEncode, List.length_append, List.length_drop, List.length_take,
      List.length_nil, pairFstD_pairEncode]
    omega
  have hl := polyTimeComputable_forLoop hs 3 2 (forLoop_bound_of_ctx 2 hctx hlen)
  exact (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_slot3).comp
    (hl.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode
      (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_const [])))))

end BinArith

end Complexity
```


## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/Encoding/BooleanVector.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.BinaryArith
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.Modular
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.CollectionsLemmas
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.Loops

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Binary domain words as encoded modular vectors

## Main definitions

* `expandStep`: append a fixed-width numeral for the next raw bit, defaulting false.
* `expandPoly`: run the existing counted loop at fixed polynomial count and width.

## Main results

The raw output length is exact. Its values are the modular zero/one vector of the
original prefix, with false defaults and excess bits ignored. The efficiency sketch
uses existing leaf contracts and the public counted loop. The step is polynomial-time.
The wrapper's efficiency proof awaits the loop registry and head-envelope disposition.

## References

* [Pei16] C. Peikert, *A Decade of Lattice Cryptography*, 17 February 2016,
  Equation (4.1.1) (the binary hash domain).
* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, 3rd ed., January 2010,
  Section 2.1 (binary representations and machine tapes).

This is representation glue, with no new sampler, hardness assumption or generic
block-traversal host. The polynomial schedules are fixed before the machine is chosen.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.BooleanVector

open Complexity Turing
open BinaryArith

/-- Consume one bit with a false default and append its normalized full-width numeral. -/
def expandStep (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  let c := pairFstD z
  let bits := pairFstD (pairSndD z)
  let out := pairSndD (pairSndD z)
  pairEncode c (pairEncode (bits.drop 1)
    (out ++ normalizeWidthPoly .var (pairEncode c [bits.headD false])))

/-- The complete expansion step appends precisely the normalized numeral of the next bit. -/
theorem expandStep_eq (z : List Bool) :
    expandStep z =
      let c := pairFstD z
      let bits := pairFstD (pairSndD z)
      let out := pairSndD (pairSndD z)
      pairEncode c (pairEncode (bits.drop 1)
        (out ++ normalizeWidthPoly .var (pairEncode c [bits.headD false]))) := rfl

/-- The expansion step preserves the full width context.

**Proof sketch.** Read the step equation and the public pair-first equation. -/
theorem expandStep_fst (z : List Bool) : pairFstD (expandStep z) = pairFstD z := by
  rw [expandStep_eq, pairFstD_pairEncode]

/-- The expansion step grows by a linear function of the width context.

**Proof sketch.** The raw bit suffix shrinks and the output gains exactly the
retained width. Public pairing lengths cover malformed inner framing with slack eight. -/
theorem expandStep_length_le (z : List Bool) :
    (expandStep z).length ≤ z.length + 8 * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) := by
  have houter := length_pair_components_le z
  have hinner := length_pair_components_le (pairSndD z)
  simp only [expandStep_eq, length_pairEncode, List.length_drop, List.length_append,
    normalizeWidthPoly_length, pairFstD_pairEncode, PolyExpr.eval_var]
  omega

/-- The bit-expansion step is polynomial-time.

**Proof sketch.** Compose public total projections, head/default singleton, drop,
append and pairing contracts with `normalizeWidthPoly .var`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_expandStep : PolyTimeComputable expandStep := by
  have hc := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD
  have hbits := BinArith.polyTimeComputable_slot2
  have hout := BinArith.polyTimeComputable_slot3
  have hnext := (polyTimeComputable_normalizeWidthPoly .var).comp
    (hc.pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_headD.comp hbits))
  have hdrop := polyTimeComputable_tail.comp hbits
  have heq := funext expandStep_eq
  exact heq.symm ▸ hc.pairEncode (hdrop.pairEncode (hout.append hnext))

/-- Write one modular residue per declared raw prefix bit, using fixed polynomial
count and width schedules and the original public counted-loop host. -/
def expandPoly (M W : PolyExpr) (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  let u := pairFstD z
  let c := List.replicate (W.eval u.length) false
  let init := pairEncode c (pairEncode (pairSndD z) [])
  let done := pairSndD (BinArith.forLoop expandStep
    (pairEncode (List.replicate (M.eval u.length) true) init))
  pairSndD (pairSndD done)

/-- The complete wrapper starts with empty output and executes the declared bit count. -/
theorem expandPoly_eq (M W : PolyExpr) (z : List Bool) :
    expandPoly M W z =
      let u := pairFstD z
      let c := List.replicate (W.eval u.length) false
      let init := pairEncode c (pairEncode (pairSndD z) [])
      let done := pairSndD (BinArith.forLoop expandStep
        (pairEncode (List.replicate (M.eval u.length) true) init))
      pairSndD (pairSndD done) := rfl

/-- Expansion writes exactly count times width bits on arbitrary raw inputs.

**Proof sketch.** Each loop round appends exactly the width and the initial output
is empty. The finite counter terminates even when count or width is zero. -/
theorem expandPoly_length (M W : PolyExpr) (z : List Bool) :
    (expandPoly M W z).length = M.eval (pairFstD z).length * W.eval (pairFstD z).length := by
  let c := List.replicate (W.eval (pairFstD z).length) false
  let init := pairEncode c (pairEncode (pairSndD z) [])
  have h (k : ℕ) :
      pairFstD ((expandStep^[k]) init) = c ∧
      (pairSndD (pairSndD ((expandStep^[k]) init))).length = k * c.length := by
    induction k with
    | zero => simp [init]
    | succ k ih =>
      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
      refine ⟨(expandStep_fst _).trans ih.1, ?_⟩
      simp only [expandStep_eq, pairSndD_pairEncode, List.length_append,
        normalizeWidthPoly_length, pairFstD_pairEncode, PolyExpr.eval_var, ih.1, ih.2,
        Nat.succ_mul]
  simp only [expandPoly_eq, BinArith.forLoop_pairEncode, List.length_replicate, pairSndD_pairEncode]
  simpa only [c, List.length_replicate] using (h (M.eval (pairFstD z).length)).2

/-- Expansion agrees with the canonical modular vector of the actual raw padded prefix.

**Proof sketch.** Induct over the counted bits, recording the emitted blocks at
successive raw head/default positions. The public padded-word equation identifies
those bits with `padFin`. The residue reader and the numeral's modular invariance
also give the required block when the width is zero. -/
theorem expandPoly_encode {q : ℕ} [NeZero q] (M W : PolyExpr) (u raw : List Bool)
    (hq : q = 2 ^ (W.eval u.length)) :
    expandPoly M W (pairEncode u raw) = Modular.encodeVector (W.eval u.length)
      (fun i : Fin (M.eval u.length) => ((padFin (M.eval u.length) raw i).toNat : ZMod q)) := by
  let width := W.eval u.length
  let c := List.replicate width false
  let block (bit : Bool) := Candidates.natToList width ((bit.toNat : ZMod q).val)
  have hblock (bit : Bool) : normalizeWidthPoly .var (pairEncode c [bit]) = block bit := by
    have hvalue : NumberTheory.listToNat [bit] = bit.toNat := by
      cases bit <;> simp [NumberTheory.listToNat_cons, NumberTheory.listToNat_nil]
    rw [normalizeWidthPoly_pairEncode, hvalue, PolyExpr.eval_var, List.length_replicate]
    dsimp only [block]
    rw [ZMod.val_natCast, hq, Candidates.natToList_mod_two_pow]
  have walk (k : ℕ) (word out : List Bool) :
      (expandStep^[k]) (pairEncode c (pairEncode word out)) =
        pairEncode c (pairEncode (word.drop k)
          (out ++ (List.ofFn fun i : Fin k => block ((word.drop i.val).headD false)).flatten)) := by
    induction k generalizing word out with
    | zero => simp
    | succ k ih =>
      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply, expandStep_eq]
      simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, hblock, ih, List.ofFn_succ,
        List.flatten_cons, Fin.val_zero, Fin.val_succ, List.drop_zero, List.drop_drop,
        Nat.add_comm 1, List.append_assoc]
  have hbit (i : Fin (M.eval u.length)) : (raw.drop i.val).headD false =
      padFin (M.eval u.length) raw i := by
    have h := congrArg (fun w : List Bool => (w[i.val]?).getD false)
      (ofFn_padFin_eq_take (M.eval u.length) raw)
    simp only [List.getElem?_ofFn, dif_pos i.isLt, Option.getD_some,
      List.getElem?_take_of_lt i.isLt] at h
    rw [List.headD_eq_head?_getD, List.head?_eq_getElem?, List.getElem?_drop, Nat.add_zero, h]
    by_cases hi : i.val < raw.length
    · rw [List.getElem?_append_left hi]
    · rw [List.getElem?_eq_none_iff.mpr (Nat.le_of_not_lt hi),
        List.getElem?_append_right (Nat.le_of_not_lt hi), List.getElem?_replicate]
      split <;> rfl
  simp only [expandPoly_eq, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, BinArith.forLoop_pairEncode,
    List.length_replicate]
  change pairSndD (pairSndD ((expandStep^[M.eval u.length]) (pairEncode c (pairEncode raw [])))) = _
  rw [walk]
  simp only [pairSndD_pairEncode, List.nil_append, hbit, block, width, Modular.encodeVector_eq]

/-- Every fixed polynomial bit-expansion schedule is polynomial-time.

**Proof sketch.** Use the retained-context envelope with `forLoop_bound_of_ctx 8`
and `polyTimeComputable_forLoop`, generate templates with existing zero/unary polynomial
machines, and compose total projections. No new host or runtime polynomial is needed. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_expandPoly (M W : PolyExpr) : PolyTimeComputable (expandPoly M W) := by
  sorry

end TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.BooleanVector
```


## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/Encoding/DyadicLinearAlgebra.lean =====

```text
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.DyadicArithmetic
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.Modular
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.Loops

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Encoded dyadic dot products and matrix-vector multiplication

## Main definitions

* `dotStep`, `dotWords`, `dotPoly`: consume fixed-width blocks in the existing counted loop.
* `matVecStep`, `matVecPoly`: consume row-major matrix rows with that same public host.

## Main results

Raw output widths are unconditional. Canonical encodings correspond to modular dot
products and matrix-vector multiplication. The dot leaf step is polynomial-time.
The loop-dependent efficiency proofs await the registry and head-envelope disposition.

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, 3rd ed., January 2010,
  Section 2.1 (machine representations).
* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*, 2009,
  Section 7.2 (polynomial-time randomized computation, model context).
* [Pei16] C. Peikert, *A Decade of Lattice Cryptography*, 17 February 2016,
  Definitions 4.1.1 and 4.2.3 (the modular products being represented).

These algorithms are repository adaptations assembled from scalar arithmetic and
`Complexity.BinArith.forLoop`; no new traversal host is defined. Counters and retained
width words have explicit polynomial lengths. Short raw final blocks are read as their
ordinary MSB numeral, hence with implicit leading zeros; this is not a claim that the
flat operand is padded at its end. Malformed pairs use the existing total projections.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.Encoding.DyadicLinearAlgebra

open Complexity Turing
open DyadicArithmetic

/-- Consume one coordinate pair and update the modular accumulator, retaining the
width word. This is the leaf step for the public counted-loop dot product. -/
def dotStep (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  let c := pairFstD z
  let xs := pairFstD (pairSndD z)
  let ys := pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD z))
  let acc := pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD z))
  pairEncode c (pairEncode (xs.drop c.length)
    (pairEncode (ys.drop c.length)
      (addPoly .var (pairEncode c (pairEncode acc
        (mulPoly .var (pairEncode c
          (pairEncode (xs.take c.length) (ys.take c.length)))))))))

/-- The complete step drops one width block per operand and adds their modular product. -/
theorem dotStep_eq (z : List Bool) :
    dotStep z =
      let c := pairFstD z
      let xs := pairFstD (pairSndD z)
      let ys := pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD z))
      let acc := pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD z))
      pairEncode c (pairEncode (xs.drop c.length)
        (pairEncode (ys.drop c.length)
          (addPoly .var (pairEncode c (pairEncode acc
            (mulPoly .var (pairEncode c
              (pairEncode (xs.take c.length) (ys.take c.length))))))))) := rfl

/-- The dot step preserves its entire width context, including on malformed input.

**Proof sketch.** Read the complete step equation and the public pair-first equation. -/
theorem dotStep_fst (z : List Bool) : pairFstD (dotStep z) = pairFstD z := by
  rw [dotStep_eq, pairFstD_pairEncode]

/-- One dot step grows by at most eight times the width-context size plus one.

**Proof sketch.** The two operands only shrink. Scalar arithmetic writes exactly the
retained width, even on malformed data. Expand public pairing lengths and bound any
framing repair by the stated slack; no numeric operand value enters the bound. -/
theorem dotStep_length_le (z : List Bool) :
    (dotStep z).length ≤ z.length + 8 * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) := by
  have houter := length_pair_components_le z
  have hmiddle := length_pair_components_le (pairSndD z)
  have hinner := length_pair_components_le (pairSndD (pairSndD z))
  simp only [dotStep_eq, length_pairEncode, List.length_drop, addPoly_length,
    pairFstD_pairEncode, PolyExpr.eval_var]
  omega

/-- The dot-product leaf step is polynomial-time, with no runtime polynomial argument.

**Proof sketch.** Compose total projections, `pairTakePoly .var` and
`pairDropPoly .var`, pairing,
and the already proved scalar `addPoly .var` and `mulPoly .var` contracts. The width
template is the retained word itself, so the per-step output bound is linear in it. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_dotStep : PolyTimeComputable dotStep := by
  have hc := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD
  have hx := BinArith.polyTimeComputable_slot2
  have hy := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp BinArith.polyTimeComputable_slot3
  have hacc := BinArith.polyTimeComputable_slot4
  have hxTake := (polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly .var).comp (hc.pairEncode hx)
  have hyTake := (polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly .var).comp (hc.pairEncode hy)
  have hxDrop := (polyTimeComputable_pairDropPoly .var).comp (hc.pairEncode hx)
  have hyDrop := (polyTimeComputable_pairDropPoly .var).comp (hc.pairEncode hy)
  have hproduct := (polyTimeComputable_mulPoly .var).comp
    (hc.pairEncode (hxTake.pairEncode hyTake))
  have hsum := (polyTimeComputable_addPoly .var).comp
    (hc.pairEncode (hacc.pairEncode hproduct))
  convert hc.pairEncode (hxDrop.pairEncode (hyDrop.pairEncode hsum)) using 1
  funext z
  simp only [dotStep_eq, Function.comp_apply, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode,
    PolyExpr.eval_var]

/-- Run one dot step per letter of `n`, starting with a zero accumulator of width `|c|`.
Only the lengths of the two template words are used. -/
def dotWords (c n x y : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  let init := pairEncode c (pairEncode x (pairEncode y (List.replicate c.length false)))
  let done := pairSndD (BinArith.forLoop dotStep (pairEncode n init))
  pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD done))

/-- The complete dot loop initializes width-many zeros and extracts the final accumulator. -/
theorem dotWords_eq (c n x y : List Bool) :
    dotWords c n x y =
      let init := pairEncode c (pairEncode x (pairEncode y (List.replicate c.length false)))
      let done := pairSndD (BinArith.forLoop dotStep (pairEncode n init))
      pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD done)) := rfl

/-- The dot loop always writes exactly the width word's length.

**Proof sketch.** At zero iterations the initialized accumulator has that length.
Each later step replaces it with the fixed-width scalar sum. Use the public counted
loop equation, including when the count or width is zero. -/
theorem dotWords_length (c n x y : List Bool) : (dotWords c n x y).length = c.length := by
  let init := pairEncode c (pairEncode x (pairEncode y (List.replicate c.length false)))
  have h (k : ℕ) :
      pairFstD ((dotStep^[k]) init) = c ∧
      (pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD ((dotStep^[k]) init)))).length = c.length := by
    induction k with
    | zero => simp [init]
    | succ k ih =>
      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
      refine ⟨(dotStep_fst _).trans ih.1, ?_⟩
      simp only [dotStep_eq, pairSndD_pairEncode, addPoly_length,
        pairFstD_pairEncode, PolyExpr.eval_var, ih.1]
  simp only [dotWords_eq, BinArith.forLoop_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode]
  exact (h n.length).2

/-- The packed four-argument dot loop is polynomial-time on all raw words.

**Proof sketch.** Apply `forLoop_bound_of_ctx 8` to the retained-context and growth
lemmas, then `polyTimeComputable_forLoop` with envelope constants nine and two.
Initialize zeros and compose the final projections with the existing FP calculus. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_dotWords : PolyTimeComputable
    (fun z => dotWords (pairFstD z) (pairFstD (pairSndD z))
      (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD z))) (pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD z)))) := by
  sorry

/-- Fix polynomial coordinate and residue-width schedules before selecting a dot machine. -/
def dotPoly (N W : PolyExpr) (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  dotWords (List.replicate (W.eval (pairFstD z).length) false)
    (List.replicate (N.eval (pairFstD z).length) true)
    (pairFstD (pairSndD z)) (pairSndD (pairSndD z))

/-- The complete wrapper derives both loop templates from the parameter word's length. -/
theorem dotPoly_eq (N W : PolyExpr) (z : List Bool) :
    dotPoly N W z =
      dotWords (List.replicate (W.eval (pairFstD z).length) false)
        (List.replicate (N.eval (pairFstD z).length) true)
        (pairFstD (pairSndD z)) (pairSndD (pairSndD z)) := rfl

/-- The polynomial dot wrapper has its declared width on every raw input.

**Proof sketch.** Apply `dotWords_length` and the public replicate-length equation. -/
theorem dotPoly_length (N W : PolyExpr) (z : List Bool) :
    (dotPoly N W z).length = W.eval (pairFstD z).length := by
  simp only [dotPoly_eq, dotWords_length, List.length_replicate]

/-- On canonical full-width vectors the loop writes their modular inner product
[Pei16, Definitions 4.1.1 and 4.2.3, representation correspondence].

**Proof sketch.** Induct over the counted coordinates. Read `Modular.encodeVector_eq`
and use public list flatten/drop/take equations for the next canonical blocks;
scalar multiplication and addition preserve the running
sum in `ZMod q`. At termination the accumulator is the canonical fixed-width numeral. -/
theorem dotPoly_encodeVector {q : ℕ} [NeZero q] (N W : PolyExpr) (u : List Bool)
    (hq : q = 2 ^ (W.eval u.length))
    (a b : Fin (N.eval u.length) → ZMod q) :
    dotPoly N W (pairEncode u
      (pairEncode (Modular.encodeVector (W.eval u.length) a)
        (Modular.encodeVector (W.eval u.length) b))) =
      Candidates.natToList (W.eval u.length) (∑ i, a i * b i).val := by
  let width := W.eval u.length
  let c := List.replicate width false
  let numeral (x : ZMod q) := Candidates.natToList width x.val
  have hlength (x : ZMod q) : (numeral x).length = c.length := by
    simp only [numeral, Candidates.length_natToList, c, List.length_replicate]
  have hread (x : ZMod q) : NumberTheory.listToNat (numeral x) = x.val :=
    Candidates.listToNat_natToList (by rw [show 2 ^ width = q from hq.symm]; exact ZMod.val_lt x)
  have hmul (x y : ZMod q) :
      mulPoly .var (pairEncode c (pairEncode (numeral x) (numeral y))) = numeral (x * y) := by
    simp only [mulPoly_pairEncode, hread, PolyExpr.eval_var, c, List.length_replicate]
    dsimp only [numeral]
    rw [ZMod.val_mul, congrArg (fun modulus => x.val * y.val % modulus) hq,
      Candidates.natToList_mod_two_pow]
  have hadd (x y : ZMod q) :
      addPoly .var (pairEncode c (pairEncode (numeral x) (numeral y))) = numeral (x + y) := by
    simp only [addPoly_pairEncode, hread, PolyExpr.eval_var, c, List.length_replicate]
    dsimp only [numeral]
    rw [ZMod.val_add, congrArg (fun modulus => (x.val + y.val) % modulus) hq,
      Candidates.natToList_mod_two_pow]
  have hzero : List.replicate width false = numeral 0 := by
    simpa only [numeral, ZMod.val_zero, List.length_replicate,
      Candidates.listToNat_replicate_false] using
      (Candidates.natToList_length_listToNat (List.replicate width false)).symm
  have walk (k : ℕ) (x y : Fin k → ZMod q) (acc : ZMod q) :
      (dotStep^[k]) (pairEncode c (pairEncode (Modular.encodeVector width x)
          (pairEncode (Modular.encodeVector width y) (numeral acc)))) =
        pairEncode c (pairEncode [] (pairEncode [] (numeral (acc + ∑ i, x i * y i)))) := by
    induction k generalizing acc with
    | zero => simp [Modular.encodeVector_eq]
    | succ k ih =>
      have hsplit (v : Fin (k + 1) → ZMod q) : Modular.encodeVector width v =
          numeral (v 0) ++ Modular.encodeVector width (fun i : Fin k => v i.succ) := by
        rw [Modular.encodeVector_eq, List.ofFn_succ, List.flatten_cons, Modular.encodeVector_eq]
      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply, dotStep_eq]
      simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, hsplit,
        List.drop_left' (hlength (x 0)), List.drop_left' (hlength (y 0)),
        List.take_left' (hlength (x 0)), List.take_left' (hlength (y 0)), hmul, hadd]
      rw [ih, Fin.sum_univ_succ, add_assoc]
  simp only [dotPoly_eq, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, dotWords_eq,
    BinArith.forLoop_pairEncode, List.length_replicate]
  change pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD ((dotStep^[N.eval u.length])
    (pairEncode c (pairEncode (Modular.encodeVector width a)
      (pairEncode (Modular.encodeVector width b) (List.replicate width false))))))) = _
  rw [hzero, walk]
  simp only [pairSndD_pairEncode, zero_add, numeral, width]

/-- Every fixed polynomial dot schedule has a polynomial-time implementation.

**Proof sketch.** Generate the width template with the existing polynomial
zero-word machine and the counter with `polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly`, then compose the
packed `dotWords` machine. The polynomials are fixed outside the machine choice. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_dotPoly (N W : PolyExpr) : PolyTimeComputable (dotPoly N W) := by
  sorry

/-- Consume one matrix row, append its modular dot product, and retain width, column
count and the full input vector as the outer loop's context. -/
def matVecStep (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  let ctx := pairFstD z
  let c := pairFstD ctx
  let n := pairFstD (pairSndD ctx)
  let v := pairSndD (pairSndD ctx)
  let rows := pairFstD (pairSndD z)
  let out := pairSndD (pairSndD z)
  let rowWidth := n.length * c.length
  pairEncode ctx (pairEncode (rows.drop rowWidth)
    (out ++ dotWords c n (rows.take rowWidth) v))

/-- The complete row step uses a row of `|n|*|c|` bits and appends one width-sized result. -/
theorem matVecStep_eq (z : List Bool) :
    matVecStep z =
      let ctx := pairFstD z
      let c := pairFstD ctx
      let n := pairFstD (pairSndD ctx)
      let v := pairSndD (pairSndD ctx)
      let rows := pairFstD (pairSndD z)
      let out := pairSndD (pairSndD z)
      let rowWidth := n.length * c.length
```
