The direct symmetric scheme is the elementary noisy-inner-product encryption obtained
from the LWE distribution: add the encoded bit to a fresh sample's last coordinate.
Wu24 Definition 20.5 and Lecture 21 provide an instructor-hosted source anchor. The notes
describe themselves as lightly edited; their mathematical details still need independent
checking at that construction's gate. This is not the generic PRF construction.

## Foundation decisions

### D1. Explicit dimensions, modulus, noise and sample count

The asymptotic security parameter is separate from LWE dimension, sample count, and
modulus. Numeric parameters form a bundle with modulus at least two. The first ideal
experiment uses a uniform secret in `(ZMod q)^n`, a uniform `m`-by-`n` matrix, and
independent coordinate errors. A single secret is shared across all `m` rows. Sampling
fresh secrets per row would state a different problem and is forbidden.

Hardness for one sample-count schedule and hardness for every polynomial schedule are
distinct predicates. No sample-extension, small-secret, normal-form, modulus-switching,
or noise-change equivalence is implicit. Parameters alone do not assert hardness.
The public predicates are `LWE.DLWEAssumption` and `SIS.SISAssumption`, following the
user's naming decision; the `D` explicitly identifies decisional LWE.

### D2. Noise laws versus implementations

The first implementation-facing model is a scalar integer sampler from a finite,
nonempty uniform seed type. It specifies its induced noise law, not uniform noise on
its support: repeated seed images retain their multiplicities. Taking an independent
seed per coordinate gives the product law. Bit samplers are an additional refinement;
efficient samplability is a separate machine obligation.

The first executable profiles use power-of-two moduli and explicit bit samplers for
the scalar noise. Fixed-length unbiased coins cannot exactly implement uniform
residues modulo an odd modulus or an arbitrary rational finite-seed noise law. General
moduli remain part of the mathematical problem; a general-modulus implementation must
account for its sampling error explicitly.

This model expresses finite rational laws. It does not claim to sample an infinite
discrete Gaussian exactly. A Gaussian-to-bounded implementation, if used, needs an
explicit statistical-distance lemma, a tail bound and an implemented sampler. The
hardness hypothesis always names the actual error law or an explicitly proved transfer.

### D3. Perfect correctness

Existing encryption structures require correctness for every coin string. Use bounded
errors and quantitative modulus conditions sufficient for this stronger guarantee.
For an even modulus, `|e| <= B` and `m B < q/4` are sufficient for the PKE subset sum;
the symmetric scheme only needs the corresponding one-error bound. The final statement
must handle the encoding distance for arbitrary allowed moduli, ties, and finite small
parameters explicitly. A negligible-error Gaussian theorem does not inhabit the existing
perfect-correctness structure without an additional argument.

For nearest-codepoint decoding with encoded bit one at `floor(q/2)`, sufficient strict
bounds are `2B < floor(q/2)` for the symmetric scheme and
`2mB < floor(q/2)` for PKE. For example, at odd modulus five, error one can produce a
tie even though it is less than `q/4`. The initial dyadic profiles avoid that boundary.

### D4. SIS is an independent assumption

Use integer solution vectors, required to be nonzero over the integers, with a squared
Euclidean norm bound. Naming the bound as `sqNormBound` avoids a hidden square root:
`sum_i z_i^2 <= sqNormBound`. The kernel equation is evaluated modulo `q`.

For the binary-domain hash, compression needs `2^m > q^n`; a collision difference has
entries in `{-1,0,1}` and squared norm at most `m`. The assumption used by that theorem
must cover this bound. Nonvacuity and exclusion of trivial solutions are checked
separately; in particular a bound admitting `q` times a coordinate vector is unsuitable.
No SIS--LWE or worst-case-lattice theorem is used or asserted.

### D5. PRG seed accounting and indexing

The first direct generator theorem has an explicit bit sampler for each error and an
exact fixed-width representation of residues; power-of-two moduli give a first exact
implementation. If each residue uses `k` bits and each scalar error uses `r` seed bits,
then sampling `(A,s,e)` uses `(mn+n)k + mr` bits and publishing `(A,As+e)` uses
`(mn+m)k` bits. Expansion requires `m(k-r) > nk`.

This inequality is a hypothesis on the actual noise sampler, not merely its support
size or Shannon entropy. A Gaussian sampler with wasteful randomness does not meet it
automatically. The final `PRG` bridge also accounts for the existing API's actual seed
length, polynomial parameter schedules, unused seed bits, output truncation to a fixed
syntactic stretch, and finite exceptional lengths. No unproved OWF-to-PRG theorem or
search-LWE reduction is substituted for these obligations.

The seed-length schedule must be increasing and efficiently computable, with polynomial
bounds on its value and its next value, so selecting the largest fitting profile does
not lose the polynomial relationship between the profile index and the actual seed
length. Independence of copied unused bits and the reindexing of nonuniform adversaries
are explicit bridge obligations.

### D6. Cryptographic trapdoors and CCA2

The allowed LWE trapdoor is a secret matrix for decoding a concealed gadget encoding.
Lossy and all-but-one function contracts are generic and public before the consumer's
fill. They need quantitative lossiness, indistinguishability, inversion and encoding
contracts. No private one-off trapdoor abstraction is built inside CCA2.

PW10 Theorem 4.2 also requires a *strongly* unforgeable one-time signature. Ordinary
fresh-message one-time security is insufficient: a new signature on the same signed
tuple can produce a different challenge-key ciphertext. Expose this stronger supporting
contract and construct an instance from the LWE-derived primitives. An intermediate
conditional theorem is allowed, but the headline LWE-only CCA2 theorem must discharge
this dependency; the independent SIS assumption must not leak into it silently.

The source review identified a signature-size cycle in raw Lamport: the signed tuple
grows with the ABO width, while its uncompressed Lamport verification key is longer
than that width. Merely increasing the ABO width does not fix this. A proposed route is
fixed-block LWE-only CRH from lossy functions (PW10 section 3.4.3), canonical domain
extension, then hash-and-Lamport using the perfectly injective trapdoor evaluator.
Injectivity gives unique signatures for a fixed digest. Hash security and inversion
security cover the remaining strong-forgery cases. The hash and signature parameters
must be independent of the eventual ciphertext length, and the ABO width must be chosen
after the resulting verification-key width is bounded. This remains a design/proof
obligation, not a claimed construction or gate closure.

PW10's lattice functions are originally almost-always injective/invertible. The existing
PKE correctness requirement must be met by an explicit bounded-noise specialization or
another checked argument, not by ignoring the bad-key event. The CCA proof retains the
full ciphertext's signature verification, inversion, canonical parsing, recomputation
checks and exact challenge-ciphertext exclusion.

A proposed exact dyadic specialization takes gadget moduli dividing the LWE modulus,
so encoding is a group homomorphism. The source review gives candidate deterministic
inversion and image-cardinality inequalities under bounded errors; these must be proved
in the statement/fill sequence. PW10's original almost-always Gaussian theorems are not
relabeled as perfect-correctness results. The ABO anti-cyclic branch matrix is inverted
over the rationals, not modulo the LWE modulus, so its role must not impose an unstated
prime-modulus assumption.

### D7. Efficiency and reuse

Use existing `Complexity.NUPPT`, `PolyExpr`, bit encodings, probability, game and machine
hosts. Do not change their public interfaces without proposing the exact diff to the
user. `Candidates.ArithmeticFP` is existing conditional arithmetic infrastructure; it is
not evidence that unconditional binary-arithmetic machines have been constructed.
Before efficiency gates, inventory the needed arithmetic/loop rows and explicitly
identify any residual hypothesis. A conditional endpoint must be labelled as such.

Reuse `InformationTheory.LeftoverHash` rather than reproving the leftover hash lemma.
The required binary-subset linear family still needs its own universality proof.

## Source freeze and proof review

The Lean diff from the passed Gate 12 snapshot is confined to five files. The other 148 indexed source paths, the root exports, and the build pins match byte for byte. The two rank bodies and seven consumer bodies replace exactly nine `sorry` stubs with their signatures preserved. Rank adds the disclosed `AdjoinRoot` and `Cyclotomic.Roots` imports. I independently enumerated the 220 frozen declarations across 19 modules. [Rank commit](https://github.com/Shilun-Allan-Li/tcslib/commit/75a4214dc098cd6c363d00c34f569bac23eb4555) · [Consumer commit](https://github.com/Shilun-Allan-Li/tcslib/commit/713093c36ac66f7e56e9354581f0bb3f59772341)

Applying the approved four-line patch to the exact parent reproduces `RandomBits.lean` at the isolated reader commit and the final pin. `Randomized.blockVal_eq` is a complete non-simp equation, by `rfl`, for `bitsVal` of the width-`b` slice at offset `i*b`. It has an empty axiom set. [Reader commit](https://github.com/Shilun-Allan-Li/tcslib/commit/2414fd3eae05c99474d1888609b01ac5989523a5)

| Checked fills | Finding |
|---|---|
| `AllButOne.antiCyclic_mulVec_injective`, `branch_difference_injective` | The quotient by the rational cyclotomic polynomial of order `2^(u+1)` gives the power basis for width `2^u`. A wrapped column index picks up the minus sign from the width-th power of the root. Reindexing the row sum identifies the transpose action with field multiplication. The power basis detects nonzero integer coefficients and lets cancellation recover each coefficient. At `u=0` the polynomial is `X+1` and the single row needs no wrap. Distinct Boolean branches give a nonzero integer difference. [Rank proofs](https://github.com/Shilun-Allan-Li/tcslib/blob/713093c36ac66f7e56e9354581f0bb3f59772341/TCSlib/Cryptography/TrapdoorFunctions/AllButOne/AntiCyclic.lean#L70) |
| `Lossy.digits_val`, `gadget_mulVec` | The slice has length `b`. Its position `k` is row-major index `j*b+k`. Reindexing the existing little-endian sum gives the exact digit, and the gadget transpose retains exactly the matching block. For `b=0` the sum is empty and the digit is zero. At `w=0` there is no digit coordinate. [Gadget proofs](https://github.com/Shilun-Allan-Li/tcslib/blob/713093c36ac66f7e56e9354581f0bb3f59772341/TCSlib/Cryptography/TrapdoorFunctions/Lossy/Gadget.lean#L183) |
| `Lossy.residual_injectiveKey`, `recover_evaluate`, `evaluate_injective` | `residual_conceal` removes the secret product. `encode_intCast` commutes the exact scale through the gadget product and leaves the original signed error sum. Its magnitude is at most `w*b*B`. Strict separation `2*(w*b*B) < 2^a` permits `decode_encode_add`, and the inverse block equivalence gives a left inverse for every input. This also covers an empty secret dimension. [Recovery proofs](https://github.com/Shilun-Allan-Li/tcslib/blob/713093c36ac66f7e56e9354581f0bb3f59772341/TCSlib/Cryptography/TrapdoorFunctions/Lossy/Matrix.lean#L143) |
| `AllButOne.residual_branch`, `evaluateBranch_injective` | After cancellation, the queried shift minus the designated shift gives the encoded integer branch-difference product plus the original error sum. The same strict rounding check recovers the product residue. Each signed coordinate has magnitude at most `2^u*(2^b-1) < 2^(b+u)`. Equality of residues makes the difference a multiple of `2^(b+u+1)`, and the triangle inequality makes its magnitude strictly smaller than that modulus. The integer products are equal, so rank and digit injectivity give equality of inputs. [Branch proofs](https://github.com/Shilun-Allan-Li/tcslib/blob/713093c36ac66f7e56e9354581f0bb3f59772341/TCSlib/Cryptography/TrapdoorFunctions/AllButOne/Basic.lean#L119) |

The sketches track the implemented arguments. The fills use the public readers and reuse the concealed residual and shared binary error-sum bound. Gate 12 findings F01 and F02 remain resolved. [Gate 12 disposition](https://github.com/Shilun-Allan-Li/tcslib/blob/f4b1e343061101565e9ac93b517d93fec6c4ded3/audits/lwe-sis-trapdoor-proofs-resolutions.md)

## Execution and axiom evidence

I independently replayed the exact seven-facade closure on x86-64 Linux with Lean 4.25.0 and the pinned Mathlib cache. All 144 modules produced fresh objects with zero errors and byte-identical logs. The logs contain nine owned and 17 inherited admission warnings. Compared with Gate 12, 140 module logs are byte-identical and every non-admission warning is preserved. Style reproduced zero failures and two inherited warnings over 41 files. All 178 recorded rank dependency source, archive, and object fingerprints also matched.

The independent axiom probe reproduced the log byte for byte. The 329 explicit prints and 616-constant inventory reconcile with Gate 12. All nine fills depend only on `propext`, `Quot.sound`, and `Classical.choice`. The additions are the reader and five compiler auxiliaries. `Lossy.evaluate.congr_simp` moves from `AllButOne.Basic` to `Lossy.Matrix` with the same name, kind, visibility, and axiom set. The nine owned `sorryAx` entries are exactly the remaining source stubs. [Gate 13 evidence](https://github.com/Shilun-Allan-Li/tcslib/tree/f4b1e343061101565e9ac93b517d93fec6c4ded3/briefs/lwe-sis-constructions/fills/09-gadget-inversion/evidence)

I replayed the type probe at all three pins, rebuilding the affected closures of 12 modules for rank and four for Gate 12. All 220 Gate 13 universe and type representations match rank exactly. Of these, 216 also match Gate 12 exactly. The four differences are integer ring projections in `antiCyclic_mulVec_injective`, `branch_difference_injective`, `branch_message_bound`, and `residual_branch`. Their before and after fingerprints reproduced, and independently regenerated reflexivity certificates passed the kernel with the recorded log hash. [Type evidence](https://github.com/Shilun-Allan-Li/tcslib/blob/f4b1e343061101565e9ac93b517d93fec6c4ded3/briefs/lwe-sis-constructions/fills/09-gadget-inversion/evidence/type-checks.json)

# Counted-loop host registration proposal

The exact one-row H16 diff registers the existing counted-loop FP contracts
and their clean-call envelope. It applies to the same registry blob on
draft #250, the central LWE/SIS target, and the current Pass–Shelat base.
[Proposed diff](proposed-for-loop-registration.patch) · [Pins and fingerprints](proposal.json)

`forLoop_bound_of_ctx` bounds intermediate **word lengths**. To obtain a
**machine head bound**, apply H14's `clean_install` to the already-proved
`polyTimeComputable_forLoop` contract. The clean module installs the same
loop result and first halts within its polynomial budget. `Clean.envelope`
bounds each work head by that budget throughout the run. The specialization
uses the existing public APIs and applies to every raw argument word.
[Checked specialization](evidence/HeadEnvelope.lean) · [Axiom prints](evidence/head-envelope.log)

The local probe passed with Lean 4.25.0, the manifest pins and this
worktree's own Gate 13 prerequisites. All six printed declarations use
only standard axioms. The shared-file diff consists of one registry row.
The seven efficiency fills can use the existing FP calculus, with the two
SIS CRH proofs downstream of the collision-output postprocessor.

The maintainer approved the exact diff. The registry row is applied on
draft #250 at `2055a7425549d9d0e9cbd1f4c2bb9b9a7a8aeb11`. Gate 14 reviews the entry and its existing
contracts before the counted-loop consumer proofs are integrated.
[Approval and verification](approval.json)

## ===== briefs/lwe-sis-constructions/prerequisites/02-counted-loop-registration/evidence/HeadEnvelope.lean =====

```text
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith.Loops
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.ModuleHost

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace LweSisGate14Preflight

open Complexity Turing Turing.ModuleHost

/-- The existing counted word loop can be installed as an H14 clean call
whose time budget also bounds each work head at every time. -/
theorem forLoop_clean_install_envelope {f : List Bool → List Bool}
    (hf : PolyTimeComputable f) (B b : ℕ)
    (hbound : ∀ c d j, j ≤ c.length →
      (f^[j] d).length ≤ B * ((pairEncode c d).length + 1) ^ b) :
    ∃ (M : FinTM Bool) (A d : ℕ),
      Clean M (BinArith.forLoop f) (fun _ => []) (fun n => A * (n + 1) ^ d) ∧
        ∀ (x arg : List Bool) (v : ℕ) (j : Fin M.k),
          |(M.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) M.tm.q₀ (stateWord M.k arg)) v).workTapePos j| ≤
            (A * (arg.length + 1) ^ d : ℕ) := by
  obtain ⟨M, A, d, hclean⟩ :=
    clean_install (BinArith.polyTimeComputable_forLoop hf B b hbound)
  exact ⟨M, A, d, hclean, hclean.envelope⟩

#print axioms forLoop_clean_install_envelope
#print axioms Complexity.BinArith.forLoop_pairEncode
#print axioms Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_forLoop
#print axioms Complexity.BinArith.forLoop_bound_of_ctx
#print axioms Turing.ModuleHost.clean_install
#print axioms Turing.ModuleHost.Clean.envelope

end LweSisGate14Preflight
```

 | H15 | **Block-rejection string-function host:** `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.polyTimeComputable_rejectBlocksL`, in `TCSlib/Cryptography/Candidates/Concrete.lean`. Given a parameter-dependent decidable test `E`, a polynomial-time bit test on paired parameter/value words, and polynomial-time words `par`, `kw`, `bw`, `tw`, `c`, publishes an existential polynomial-time output `g`: rejection is `g z = []`; otherwise the value is read from `(g z).tail`, whose length is at most `(kw z).length`. Sizes and trial count are the supplied words' lengths; no `k ≤ B`, positivity or full-coin-length premise is imposed. Depends on `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateFind` (the repetition host in `Randomized/Repetition.lean`, via `Build/IterateFind.lean` and the H14 clean-module host). This layer exposes polynomial time and the payload-length bound; a separate machine head-envelope clause is not exposed. | **Statement only**, in PR #227; **gate 08 CLOSED**, round 2 PASS (0 blockers/0 majors/0 minors), audited head `84f35910912bd3d1cd520beea9469e0ed45ce504`, 2026-11-06 PST. #227 was merged by the user as `31348fcf7dee32f84db1fc8f929d80653137995e`. On a paired state it runs a polynomial-time leaf once per counter letter. The caller supplies a polynomial bound on all intermediate argument words. The retained-context corollary derives this bound from context preservation and linear growth. For the same result function on every raw word, apply H14's `Turing.ModuleHost.clean_install` to `polyTimeComputable_forLoop`. Its clean call installs the result by its polynomial first-halt budget, and `Clean.envelope` bounds every work head at every time by that same budget. | Existing public proofs.
